Wider Sports News.title: SI hosts masterclass on fan engagement, unveils the Digital Fandom Quadrant
Wider Sports News.summary: SI has launched Digital Fandom Quadrant, a new framework designed to help teams, leagues and federations assess their digital maturity, build stronger direct relationships with fans, and unlock the value of owned first-party data in an AI-driven era. The post SI hosts masterclass on fan engagement, unveils the Digital Fandom Quadrant appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
For too long, Indian sport has treated fan engagement as a synonym for social-media engagement. Followers, views and likes are a starting point and not a very solid one. Teams and leagues broadcast a steady stream of content to reach millions, with little real understanding of who is on the other end. By most estimates, the vast majority of Indian sports organisations cannot identify their individual fans: the data sits on third-party apps and social platforms, owned by those platforms rather than by the organisation itself.

That gap becomes a genuine risk in an AI-driven, personalisation-first era, where an organisation’s fan engagement is only ever as good as the data it owns. This was the premise of a masterclass on the future of fan engagement hosted by Sportz Interactive (SI). The timing is pointed: with the government’s recently approved ₹36,441 crore expansion of the Khelo India programme – the largest public investment in Indian sport since Independence a bid for the 2036 Olympics, and an industry-wide push to build fandom beyond cricket, the question of how organisations actually engage their fans has never mattered more.

Wider Sports News.title: Gracenote | Sport’s age of discovery
Wider Sports News.summary: The sports streaming landscape has never been more crowded, or more confusing for fans. Nearly 1 in 2 viewers have considered cancelling a subscription over it. Explore the data on what's driving fans away, and what platforms can do about it. The post Gracenote | Sport’s age of discovery appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
50% of viewers would consider cancelling a subscription because they cannot find what they are looking for. As content splinters across an ever-growing number of platforms, sports fans are being left behind. Football alone isn’t the story here — NFL fans now need six broadcast networks and five streaming platforms just to catch every game, while nearly half of all viewers say they’d consider cancelling a subscription simply because they can’t find what they’re looking for.

Gracenote’s new whitepaper, produced in partnership with SportsPro, breaks down what this fragmentation means for sports media platforms — and what the best operators are doing to fix it.

Wider Sports News.title: Fourteen Kenyan Stars Selected for Ultimate Sevens Championship
Wider Sports News.summary: Fourteen Kenyan Stars Selected for Ultimate Sevens Championship Kenya Rugby Union
Wider Sports News.body:
Fourteen Kenyan rugby sevens stars have earned selection for the Ultimate Sevens Championship, underlining the country's growing influence on the global sevens stage. The competition, designed to bring together the world's best players,including Olympians and world champions,will be staged across four events in Madrid, Cardiff, Biarritz and London this September.The selected players, drawn from both the Kenya Shujaa and Kenya Lionesses squads, will represent six franchise teams in the new-look championship.

Clan Taran will feature the experienced trio of Vincent Onyala, John Okoth and Sheila Chajira. Onyala heads into the competition as a two-time Olympian who has also represented Kenya at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and the Rugby World Cup Sevens. Okoth, a member of Kenya's Paris 2024 Olympic squad, previously represented Kenya U20 and recently featured in India's Rugby Premier League. Joining them is Kenya Lionesses captain Sheila Chajira, a two-time Olympian who also turned out for the Chennai Bulls in this year's Rugby Premier League.

Wider Sports News.body:
Arsenal and Emirates have agreed a five-year extension to their long-running sponsorship agreement, believed to be worth up to UK£70 million a season. The airline will remain the Premier League champions’ front-of-shirt, training kit and stadium naming rights partner until 2033 in a deal that also covers Arsenal’s women’s and youth teams.

The relationship, which began in 2006, is the longest-running shirt sponsorship in the Premier League. The annual value of this latest extension represents a significant uplift on the previous contract, which is understood to be worth up to UK£50 million annually.

From next season, DAZN will be the exclusive direct-to-consumer (DTC) home of the New York area MSG Networks and YES Network regional sports networks (RSNs), with the Gotham Sports App joint-venture shut down.

Rugby.body:
Wallabies prop Allan Alaalatoa has played 92 Tests and Rob Valetini is a two-time recipient of the John Eales Medal. But Declan Meredith hasn’t been overawed by the chance to play alongside some giants of Australian rugby, having become a well-respected member of the group.

Cairns-born Meredith has completed a remarkable rise from ACT club rugby in the John I Dent Cup to higher honours in Wallaby gold. The 26-year-old debuted against France last month and has started another two Tests in the No. 10 jersey since.

Rugby.title: 'Vulnerable': Steve Hansen warns Springboks over risky bench tactic
Rugby.summary: “I hear the commentators, ‘it’s changed the course of the game’, but you know that before you go in, I don’t think you can use it as an excuse for anything.
Rugby.body:
Former All Blacks head coach Steve Hansen has used the Stormers’ six-two split outcome as a warning to Rassie Erasmus and the Springboks ahead of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry. Hansen’s claim follows the Stormers’ early injuries to halfbacks Imad Khan and Dewaldt Duvenage against the All Blacks, leaving their only bench back replacement, Wandisile Simelane, and the other outside-backs to monitor the base of the ruck.

Stormers head coach John Dobson opted for the popular six-two split on the bench, carrying an extra forward to provide impact and versatility against the All Blacks. The tactic, used often at Test level by Erasmus and other Test sides, can work in the team’s advantage if everything goes to plan, and no backline players, or only one, get injured during the 80-minute contest.

Rugby.title: Wallabies lock Miles Amatosero cops suspension for dangerous ruck entry
Rugby.summary: "Amatosero was given permission to apply to take part in World Rugby's Coaching Intervention Programme as a substitute for the final match of the sanction."
Rugby.body:
Wallabies and Waratahs lock Miles Amatosero has copped a suspension for a dangerous ruck entry against Japan in Osaka. Amatosero was yellow-carded in the 33rd minute of Les Kiss’ first outing as head coach of the Wallabies for a high shot on a Japanese player at a breakdown.

Referee Eoghan Cross initially sent the lock to the sin bin before the yellow card turned red, ruling the Waratahs enforcer out of the rest of the contest. The Wallabies overcame a valiant effort from Eddie Jones’ Brave Blossoms, helped by second-half scores from Max Jorgensen, Fraser McReight, and Taniela Tupou.

Rugby.summary: Harry Godfrey has played an integral role in that early-season success, making another promising return from an injury spell.
Rugby.body:
Hawke’s Bay sit in top spot on the NPC standings after two rounds, piling on more than 100 points across commanding wins over Wellington and Tasman. Harry Godfrey has played an integral role in that early-season success, making another promising return from an injury spell.

Godfrey was made to wait 330 days between competitive matches after suffering a significant injury during a training session with the Magpies. The first five-eighth missed most of last year’s NPC season and the entire 2026 Super Rugby Pacific campaign.

Rugby.title: Joseph Suaalii move a 'first world problem' for Wallabies
Rugby.summary: Debate over the best position for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii is the "first world problem" new Wallabies coach Les Kiss will attempt to solve in a Japan rematch in Townsville.
Rugby.body:
Debate over the best position for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii is the “first world problem” new Wallabies coach Les Kiss will attempt to solve in a Japan rematch in Townsville. With Len Ikitau (ankle) injured, Suaalii and Hunter Paisami formed the midfield partnership in Australia’s hard-fought 35-32 defeat of Japan in Osaka on Saturday.

No.12 Paisami, coached by Kiss at the Queensland Reds for the last three seasons, made the most of his call-up as one of the side’s best starters alongside impressive lock Josh Canham.

Rugby.body:
Senirusi Seruvakula will stay on as Fiji acting head coach for the Pacific Nations Cup, which is scheduled to start in almost one month to the day. Fiji One News reported the update this week, including comments from Fiji Rugby Union CEO Koli Sewabu.

Rugby.title: Why Dave Rennie handed Luke Jacobson the All Blacks captaincy
Rugby.summary: "Looking forward to getting out there and to be honest, trying not to think about too deeply. Probably take the time after the game to just appreciate it."
Rugby.body:
It was all surprises when Dave Rennie read out the 23 names that would take on the Sharks in Durban, especially for Luke Jacobson, who was selected to captain the All Blacks for the first time.

The Chiefs captain led the New Zealand U20s to their last World Cup title back in 2017, but has never had the chance to lead the All Blacks in his 27 Test caps. On Wednesday morning NZT, against the Sharks in Durban, Jacobson will lead the All Blacks in the side’s second match on Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour for 2026.

Rugby.body:
Brad Mooar’s Fijian Drua have added seven-Test Flying Fijians halfback Sam Wye to their 2027 Super Rugby Pacific squad. The 25-year-old hasn’t featured in Super Rugby Pacific since 2023, with Moana Pasifika against the Hurricanes, but has played for Auckland, Counties Manukau, and Hawke’s Bay in the Hilux NPC competition.

The St Peter’s College in Auckland graduate is the son of former Fiji football international Filipe Wye, continuing his family’s sporting connection with Fiji. Wye, who made his Flying Fijians debut against Scotland at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva back in 2025, said he’s excited to represent the Fijian Drua.

Rugby.title: Gloucester decide against Villa Park return
Rugby.summary: Gloucester Rugby confirm they will not be returning to Villa Park to face Leicester Tigers in the Prem next season.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester have ditched plans to again stage next season's Prem match against Leicester Tigers at Villa Park. The club's home Slater Cup fixture was taken on the road to the home of Premier League side Aston Villa for the first time last season and drew an attendance of 24,298 as the Tigers won 36-17.

However Gloucester have decided to return to Kingsholm - which has a capacity of 16,000 - for next season's game on the weekend of 27 March, 2027. The club said the decision had been influenced by significant stadium developments planned at Villa Park over the coming months.

Rugby.title: All Blacks remove Cam Roigard from Sharks game as 'precautionary measure'
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks have removed star halfback Cam Roigard from this week's Sharks game as a "precautionary measure", noting a tight calf as the cause for concern.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks have removed star halfback Cam Roigard from this week’s Sharks game as a “precautionary measure”, noting a tight calf as the cause for concern. Roigard was named on the bench for the Sharks contest after missing the opening match of the tour, but will now be replaced in the No.21 jersey by Cortez Ratima, with Kyle Preston remaining in the starting unit for his first start in the black jersey.

The Hurricanes star had a heavy workload throughout the opening block of Nations Championship games, starting all three Tests and averaging just shy of 70 minutes per game. The game time saw him emerge from the July Tests with the most passes, carries, defenders beaten and tries of any halfback in the 12-team tournament.

Rugby.title: 'Clearly the number one': Springboks coach Erasmus shoots down Hanekom talk
Rugby.summary: Hanekom delivered a man-of-the-match performance in his second showing of the year after missing the entire 2025 season with injury.
Rugby.body:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has shot down the suggestion that there will be competition for the No.8 jersey after Cameron Hanekom’s display in Argentina. Hanekom delivered a man-of-the-match performance in his second showing of the year after missing the entire 2025 season with injury.

The 24-year-old has been a standout in the URC for the Bulls for a number of years but injuries have limited his international career to just three caps. The performance raised eyebrows for many with incumbent No.8 Jasper Wiese was left back in South Africa to prepare for the series against the All Blacks.

Rugby.title: 54th Mercantile Rugby Sevens
Rugby.summary: 54th Mercantile Rugby Sevens The Morning
Rugby.body:
The Mercantile Rugby Football Association (MRFA) has announced that the 54th Mercantile Rugby Sevens will be held from 13 to 15 November, marking the return of one of Sri Lanka’s longest-running and most popular corporate rugby sevens tournaments.

Spanning more than five decades, the Mercantile Rugby Sevens has become a prominent fixture in Sri Lanka’s corporate sporting calendar, known for its competitive spirit, camaraderie and sportsmanship.

Rugby.title: Sale Sharks co-owner makes major claim over future stadium
Rugby.summary: Sale Sharks co-owner Michelle Orange has pledged that the club will be in its own stadium within the next decade, after revealing the limited revenue it can generate from playing at its rented home.
Rugby.body:
Sale Sharks co-owner Michelle Orange has pledged that the club will be in its own stadium within the next decade, after revealing the limited revenue it can generate from playing at its rented home.

Orange told the Love of Rugby podcast that the club has to pay the owners of the CorpAcq Stadium, Salford City Council, six per cent of every ticket sold, but doesn’t earn revenue from sources such as car parking or food and drink.

Rugby.title: Bath to go on the road for Prem season run-in
Rugby.summary: Bath's last two home games of the season to be played away from The Rec as part of an accelerated construction plan for the club's new stadium.
Rugby.body:
Bath's last two home games of the season will be played away from The Rec as part of an accelerated construction plan for the club's new stadium. The new timeline, which is aimed at completing the revamped stadium for Bath in time for the start of the 2028/9 season, will see the games against Harlequins on the weekend of May 15 and Saracens on June 5 moved.

Should Bath secure a home semi-final, as they have done for the past three seasons, this will also have to be taken on the road. "We are in discussion with alternative host venues, and we will update you once the location for these fixtures is confirmed," Bath chief executive Tarquin McDonald wrote in an open letter to club supporters, external.

Rugby.title: Spain name 36-player squad as WXV Global Series Challenger preparation ramps up
Rugby.summary: A 36-player Las Leonas squad has been named as preparations for the WXV Global Series Challenger commence.
Rugby.body:
A 36-player Las Leonas squad has been named as preparations for the WXV Global Series Challenger commence. Regis Sonnes – who led Spain to a Rugby Europe Women’s Championship title in his first campaign as head coach – will see his team play Fiji, Samoa and Brazil across three consecutive weekends in Hong Kong China.

The squad includes scrum-half Anne Fernández de Corres. This season the 28-year-old turned out for the ACT Brumbies in Super Rugby Women’s and claimed the team’s Helen Taylor Award for Women’s Player of the Year at the conclusion of her debut season in Canberra.

Rugby.summary: The Ospreys are closing in on a deal with former Wallaby wing Marika Koroibete, who has been speaking to them about joining ahead of the new United Rugby Championship season...
Rugby.body:
The Ospreys are closing in on a deal with former Wallaby wing Marika Koroibete, who has been speaking to them about joining ahead of the new United Rugby Championship season, which they kick off against the Sharks at Kings Park at the end of next month.

The Ospreys already have two Australian internationals at the club, with Chiefs inside centre Lalakai Foketi joining back-rower Liam Wright in South Wales earlier this summer. They have also signed Lawson Creighton from the Waratahs.

Rugby.title: Springbok Women expressed 'freedom' in big Fijiana win
Rugby.summary: Springbok Women assistant coach Laurian Johannes-Haupt was enthused with the team's 55-12 win against Fiji in Suva on Saturday afternoon.
Rugby.body:
Springbok Women assistant coach Laurian Johannes-Haupt was enthused with the team’s 55-12 win against Fiji in Suva on Saturday afternoon. Across the 80 minutes, South Africa scores from Nombuyekezo Mdliki, Lindelwa Gwala, Vainah Ubisi, Sizophila Solontsi, Maceala Samboya, Byrhandre Dolf, Sinelitha Noxeke and a Xoliswa Khuzwayo brace put clear distance between the two teams.

Springbok captain Libbie Janse van Rensburg kicked two conversions, while Dolf converted three tries. Springbok Women Sevens star Shiniqwa Lamprecht made her Test debut as a starter in the contest.

Rugby.summary: Bath Rugby have revealed plans to bring forward the completion of their long-awaited stadium redevelopment, with chief executive Tarquin McDonald...
Rugby.body:
Bath Rugby have revealed plans to bring forward the completion of their long-awaited stadium redevelopment, with chief executive Tarquin McDonald confirming the club has submitted a planning amendment aimed at cutting the construction programme to around 18 months.

Writing in an open letter to supporters, McDonald said the club remains on course to begin construction in 2027 but believes the revised phasing could allow the new stadium to be ready for the start of the 2028/29 season.

Rugby.summary: Ireland and Lions inside-centre Robbie Henshaw could finish his career away from Leinster after being marketed as available for a move following next year’s World Cup in Australia.
Rugby.body:
Ireland and Lions inside-centre Robbie Henshaw could finish his career away from Leinster after being marketed as available for a move following next year’s World Cup in Australia.

Athlone-born Henshaw, who celebrated his 33rd birthday in June, has played over 120 games for Leinster since he joined them from Connacht a decade ago, winning four Pro 14 crowns and a United Rugby Championship title.

Rugby.summary: Wing Lisa Neumann returns from injury as head coach Sean Lynn names 14 uncapped players in a 46-strong squad preparing for four autumn Tests.
Rugby.body:
Wing Lisa Neumann returns for Wales in an extended 46-player training squad preparing for the autumn's four-match WXV Global Series. The 32-year-old, who remains unattached after leaving Harlequins in July, missed almost all of the 2026 Six Nations after suffering a hamstring injury in the opening game against Scotland.

Rugby.summary: The Sharks have lost Springbok Vincent Tshituka and Emile van Heerden from their squad for Tuesday’s Greatest Rivalry clash with the All Blacks at Hollywoodbets Kings Park.
Rugby.body:
The Sharks have lost Springbok Vincent Tshituka and second-row Emile van Heerden from their squad for Tuesday’s Greatest Rivalry clash with the All Blacks at Hollywoodbets Kings Park.

The two-cap Tshituka, who made his debut for the world champions against Italy last year, has been ruled out after suffering a reported head injury in training. Van Heerden has also been withdrawn after picking up an injury. The 6’7, 110kg 26-year-old was set to line up against the All Blacks but now Deon Slabbert has been promoted into the starting XV to partner Hendre Stassen.

Rugby.summary: Wales head coach Sean Lynn has named a 46-player extended training squad for their four-game WXV Global Series campaign.
Rugby.body:
Wales head coach Sean Lynn has named a 46-player extended training squad for their four-game WXV Global Series campaign. In total 14 uncapped players have been named in the squad. This includes Lily Hawkins, Amy Williams, Kelsie Webster, Stella Orrin and Lucy Issac, who all represented Wales in their uncapped fixture against the Barbarians at Allianz Stadium in June.

Ffion Williuams, Crystal James, Shanelle Williams and Savannah Picton Powell are more of the uncapped players named in the squad. Of the 46 players selected by Lynn, 37 have played Celtic Challenge rugby for either Brython Thunder or Gwalia Lightning.

Rugby.title: 'I can't wait to get started': Edinburgh appoint ex-Scotland international as new head coach
Rugby.summary: Scotland Under-21 coach Louise Dalgliesh has been appointed head coach of Edinburgh Rugby in the Celtic Challenge.
Rugby.body:
Scotland Under-21 coach Louise Dalgliesh has been appointed head coach of Edinburgh Rugby in the Celtic Challenge. A 67-cap Scotland international during her playing career, she joined the capital side from club partner the University of Edinburgh, where she served as Head of Performance for Women’s Rugby.

Dalgliesh replaces Claire Cruickshank at Edinburgh, who was recently appointed as Scottish Rugby’s first-ever Women’s National Academy Manager. The former Scotland international has worked for Japan Women as an assistant coach at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2021 [hosted in 2022] and as an assistant for JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby club Sale Sharks. In May 2025 Dalgliesh was appointed head coach of Scotland U20/U21.

Rugby.title: Ex-SA coach on the 3 things Springboks must fix before facing All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Nick Mallett has identified three areas South Africa can “definitely get better” in before facing the All Blacks, with the former Springboks...
Rugby.body:
Nick Mallett has identified three areas South Africa can “definitely get better” in before facing the All Blacks, with the former Springboks head coach calling for improvements in their lineout, attack and contestable kicking.

South Africa edged Argentina 17-10 in Buenos Aires on Saturday in their final match before their attention turns to New Zealand and the Greatest Rivalry. The victory at Estadio José Amalfitani was far from flawless, with Los Pumas making life uncomfortable for the world champions for large periods before the visitors eventually secured the win following a nervey final play.

Rugby.title: Rugby union's sniffiness around making money is exhausting
Rugby.summary: There has been a curious sniffiness around Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, as if South Africa and New Zealand have committed some breach of rugby etiquette by discovering...
Rugby.body:
A “branded, fundraising exercise”, according to The Times. The commercial imperatives have been “hammered home”, according to The Guardian. Elsewhere, the phrase “cash grab” has inevitably appeared.

There has been a curious sniffiness around Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, as if South Africa and New Zealand have committed some breach of rugby etiquette by discovering that people might pay good money to watch the two best teams in the world play each other.

Rugby.title: Black Ferns XV name 23-strong squad to battle Black Ferns in Wellington
Rugby.summary: Blair Baxter has included five capped Black Ferns in his Black Ferns XV squad ahead of this weekend's one-off clash.
Rugby.body:
Blair Baxter has included five capped Black Ferns in his Black Ferns XV squad ahead of this weekend’s one-off clash. On Friday afternoon, the Black Ferns XV will take on the Black Ferns at Maidstone Park in Upper Hutt, Wellington. Nine players who represented the Black Ferns XV in 2025 have been selected in Whitney Hanson’s Black Ferns squad for upcoming O’Reilly Cup, Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry and WXV Global Series fixtures.

“This is a strong squad that has a balance of talent and potential with a shared ambition of representing the Black Ferns,” Baxter said. “This fixture is a great opportunity for these players to experience what will look and feel like a Test week. It’s also a chance for us to establish a solid foundation for Black Ferns XV as we build towards the first-ever British & Irish Lions Women’s Series next year.”

Rugby.summary: Hunter Paisami is hungry for a hometown farewell as calls mount for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to switch to the wing under new Wallabies coach Les Kiss.
Rugby.body:
Hunter Paisami is hungry for a hometown farewell as calls mount for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to switch to the wing under new Wallabies coach Les Kiss. With Len Ikitau (ankle) injured, the pair formed the midfield partnership in Australia’s hard-fought 35-32 defeat of Japan in Osaka on Saturday.

Rugby.title: Wallabies won't shy away from 'license to play' under Kiss
Rugby.summary: Australia defied a 20-minute red card and brutal heat and humidity to pip Eddie Jones's plucky Japan 35-32 and ensure the Kiss era began with victory on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies won’t be spooked off the Les Kiss way after avoiding an Osaka disaster, pledging to commit after being “given a licence to play” by the new coach. Australia defied a 20-minute red card and brutal heat and humidity to pip Eddie Jones’s plucky Japan 35-32 and ensure the Kiss era began with victory on Saturday.

Flyhalf Declan Meredith battled all night to make ground with his exit kicks, and the fluency shown in a last-start flogging of Italy wasn’t there. But, after winning just five of 15 Tests under Joe Schmidt last year, they did enough and will meet Japan again in friendlier conditions in Townsville this Saturday afternoon, hoping to find a higher gear.

Rugby.summary: Stormers flanker and Springbok Deon Fourie has been called into the Springboks ahead of the Greatest Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
Stormers flanker and Springbok Deon Fourie has been called into the Springboks ahead of the Greatest Rivalry series according to a report by SA Rugby Mag. The 39-year-old was industrious for the Stormers against the All Blacks on Friday night playing openside flanker and will now potentially take on the Test team.

He provides loose forward and hooker cover for the Springboks who are awaiting scans on captain Siya Kolisi who was forced off the field early in Buenos Aires against Argentina.

Rugby.title: 'Worried': Justin Marshall flags concern for Dave Rennie after Stormers clash
Rugby.summary: "Guys like Peter Lakai really fronted up. Fabian Holland, how good was he, having not played a lot of rugby, and equally you can just see the balance of that side and players that hadn't played a lot.
Rugby.body:
Former All Black halfback Justin Marshall believes there are multiple areas of concern for Dave Rennie after their 17-point triumph over the Stormers in Cape Town. Rugby.title: Report: Scott Robertson offered shock NRL head coaching role
Rugby.summary: “The ball’s in Razor’s court at the moment, but I don’t want to push him or pressure him in any way."
Rugby.body:
The New Zealand Herald has reported that former All Blacks head coach Scott Robertson has been offered an NRL head coaching role with the Southern Orcas. The proposed Christchurch-based NRL franchise, according to club president Sir Graham Lowe, has tabled a four-year deal to Robertson to become the head coach.

The 51-year-old has been without a role since departing the All Blacks frame in January 2026, apart from a short stint with the Barbarians alongside Felipe Contepomi. “We’re well aware that he’s not coached rugby league before, but he’s certainly got a good handle on rugby league and has been looking at it closely and studying it closely for a long time; that’s quite obvious,” Lowe told the Herald.

Rugby.body:
Black Ferns head coach Whitney Hansen has revealed her 31-strong squad for the rest of 2026, making nine changes from the Pacific Four Series. Hansen’s side will take on the Black Ferns XV this Friday at Maidstone Park in Upper Hutt, before beginning to prepare for the O’Reilly Cup presented by Bupa against Australia.

Rugby.body:
Former Springbok wing Sbu Nkosi has revealed that the death of his two children at birth sat behind the mental health crisis that engulfed his time at the Vodacom Bulls and left him fearing for his own safety.

Nkosi, a member of South Africa’s 2019 Rugby World Cup-winning squad, disappeared from public view in late 2022. The Bulls said he had been absent without leave for three weeks and that their last contact with him had come on November 11, prompting a missing-person case to be opened with the South African Police Service (SAPS).

Rugby.title: Japan vs Wallabies: Dearns and Canham World XV locks, Gordon should start
Rugby.summary: The Wallabies are off to a winning start under new coach Les Kiss, overcoming a Miles Amatosero 20-minute red card in a tense 35-32 win over Japan.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies are off to a winning start under new coach Les Kiss, overcoming a Miles Amatosero 20-minute red card in a tense 35-32 win over Japan in Osaka. It’s the first time in 12 months that the Wallabies have successfully gone back-to-back with wins, following a 47-point triumph over Italy last month. They will chase more drought-breaking history next weekend, having not won three Tests in a row since the July internationals in 2024.

Next up for the Wallabies is another clash with the Brave Blossoms, with Townsville’s Queensland Country Bank Stadium hosting the fixture, 14 months out from Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 on home soil.

Rugby.title: Four major surgeries in four years: Newest Wallaby's hard-earned Osaka debut
Rugby.summary: Isaac Henry will run the prospect of fresh ink past his wife but is otherwise assured he can make a permanent Wallabies mark.
Rugby.body:
Isaac Henry will run the prospect of fresh ink past his wife but is otherwise assured he can make a permanent Wallabies mark after a hard-earned debut in Osaka. Named on the bench, the Queensland Reds centre was made to wait more than 70 minutes before being thrust into the action and then defending furiously in a 35-32 Saturday night defeat of Japan.

The 27-year-old became Wallaby No.999 in the process, the honour coming despite Henry enduring four major surgeries in as many years. “It’s a great number, might have to talk to my wife about getting it tattooed,” said Henry, who has his surname inked on his forearm.

Kyuden Voltex, who play in the Japanese league’s second tier, announced Vunilagi, 26, died on Friday morning having been taken to hospital on Monday after a training session.

Rugby.title: Fijian Vunilagi dies in Japan from suspected heatstroke
Rugby.summary: Fijian Saimoni Vunilagi has died of suspected heatstroke after a training session, his Japanese club Kyuden Voltex announce.
Rugby.body:
Fijian Saimoni Vunilagi has died of suspected heatstroke after a training session, his club Kyuden Voltex have announced. The Japanese second division team, based in Fukuoka, said the 26-year-old was taken to hospital and died on Friday, 7 August.

Temperatures in the southern city of Fukuoka this week have reached 35C degrees. "After team practice on Monday, 3 August 2026, Saimoni displayed symptoms consistent with severe heatstroke. He was transported to a medical facility for treatment, but despite the best efforts of the medical team, he sadly passed away," a team statement said.

Both Sir Steve Hansen and Eddie Jones have arrived at the same conclusion when predicting the four-Test section of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour, with both coaches expecting a series too tight to call.

Rugby.summary: The opening match of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour saw two new faces wear the black jersey for the first time, and plenty more return to it after spells away.
Rugby.body:
The opening match of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour saw two new faces wear the black jersey for the first time, and plenty more return to it after spells away. While they won’t be awarded Test caps, Josh Jacomb replaced Beauden Barrett in the 68th minute and injected some life into the attack, and Siale Lauakai came on for Pasilio Tosi after 47 minutes and was quickly subjected to the power of the Stormers’ scrum, which had the upper hand all night.

While the game was largely a dead heat for the first hour, the New Zealand bench sparked a late surge that ultimately saw the visitors emerge as 17-point victors. The debutants contributed to that surge, and head coach Dave Rennie recognised the occasion as a special one for both players.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: Ma'a Nonu named to face All Blacks in Sharks debut
Rugby.summary: In one of the more unlikely twists in rugby history, New Zealand legend Ma'a Nonu has been named to square off with the All Blacks in his Sharks debut next week.
Rugby.body:
In one of the more unlikely twists in rugby history, New Zealand legend Ma’a Nonu has been named to square off with the All Blacks in his Sharks debut next week. The midweek fixture is the second of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour, and will pit one of New Zealand’s all-time greats against the team he played 103 Tests for and won two Rugby World Cups with, as Nonu enters his 25th season as a professional rugby player.

The remarkable story comes just days after Nonu joined the club in person, having signed in a “high-performance mentorship” capacity in late July. The 44-year-old will come off the bench, with Murray Koster named to start at inside centre and rising star Jurenzo Julius in the No.13 jersey.

Rugby.summary: The Rio legacy: Why Aussie rugby sevens gold will forever have an impact ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
Rugby.body:
Shannon Parry was on a morning jog in Brisbane a few years back when she was stopped in her tracks. Running past a primary school, she noticed a group of girls, aged no more than eight years old, playing rugby.

As the co-captain of Australia's victorious women's rugby sevens team at the 2016 Olympics, Parry was struck by the sight. Parry didn't start playing rugby until she was 18 because the opportunities to do so weren't as readily available when she was younger.

Rugby.summary: Uruguay head coach Rodolfo Ambrosio and assistant coach Juan Figallo have lost their jobs just over one year out from Rugby World Cup 2027.
Rugby.body:
Uruguay head coach Rodolfo Ambrosio and assistant coach Juan Figallo have lost their jobs just over one year out from Rugby World Cup 2027. Following a disappointing opening month in the World Rugby Nations Cup, in which the team won only one game, the board reviewed the work of Ambrosio and Figallo, and both parties agreed to part ways.

Ambrosio, who had previously held the Brazilian Tupís head coach position, joined Uruguay in 2024 after Esteban Meneses opted not to extend his stay after more than a decade working with the Teros.

Rugby.title: Top 14 loosens salary cap ahead of new season
Rugby.summary: The Top 14 is set to introduce a slight financial relaxation of its Salary Cap for the 2026/27 season, which gets underway in a few weeks.
Rugby.body:
The Top 14 is set to introduce a slight financial relaxation of its Salary Cap for the 2026/27 season, which gets underway in a few weeks. The salary ceiling, which limits the total amount a club can devote to player and staff remuneration, will rise from €10.7 million to €11 million. It will then increase by €100,000 per season until it reaches €11.3 million in 2029/30.

This move further widens the financial gap between the French top flight and the Gallagher Premiership. The Premiership’s salary cap sits at £6.4 million (approximately €7.5 million) and will remain unchanged for the 2026/27 campaign, which kicks off on September 25.

Rugby.body:

Kirifi has captained the Lions to NPC titles in 2022 and 2024, and more recently helped lead the Hurricanes to a drought-breaking Super Rugby Pacific championship, but the backrower did all that with the number seven on his back.

Rugby.title: Brayden Iose on Hurricanes' 'perfect storm', Aaron Smith and Manawatu royalty
Rugby.summary: On August 28, Manawatu officially marks its 140th Anniversary with a special dinner at Central Energy Trust Arena in Palmerston North.
Rugby.body:
On August 28, Manawatu officially marks its 140th Anniversary with a special dinner at Central Energy Trust Arena in Palmerston North. For the last decade, or seven per cent of the Union’s existence, Brayden Iose has been a vital part of the furniture.

The strapping loose forward debuted in a 25-20 win against Southland on September 30, 2017, in Invercargill, a year after captaining the New Zealand Secondary Schools. He has since made 56 appearances for the Turbos, winning the Manawatu Player of the Year award three times. In 2019 he scored a try in the famous 32-29 win against Canterbury in Christchurch, Nick Croswell’s 100th game.

Rugby.title: Blues lure another rising talent north from Highlanders
Rugby.summary: The youngster ended his rookie Super Rugby Pacific campaign with three starts, including a try on debut, after replacing the injured Dylan Pledger during pre-season.
Rugby.body:
The Blues have signed halfback Nic Shearer for the 2027 season, luring the 23-year-old north after a stellar rookie season with the Highlanders. The signing comes after the Blues announced the recruitment of Otago and Highlanders first-five Cam Millar last month, plugging the impending gap to be left by Stephen Perofeta when the All Black makes the move to Japan later this year.

The Blues have also recently re-signed halfback Taufa Funaki, while both Finlay Christie and Sam Nock are off contract at the end of this year. Shearer, who had two seasons of NPC under his belt, one for Canterbury and one for Southland, when he made his Super Rugby debut this March, said he was thrilled to be heading to the City of Sails to be a part of incoming head coach Jason Holland’s game plan.

Rugby.title: Reshuffle required as Wallace Sititi withdraws from All Blacks' tour opener
Rugby.summary: Wallace Sititi has withdrawn from the opening match of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour due to illness, and will be replaced in the starting team by All Blacks rookie Anton Segner.
Rugby.body:
Wallace Sititi has withdrawn from the opening match of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour due to illness, and will be replaced in the starting team by All Blacks rookie Anton Segner.

The late scratch has triggered a minor reshuffle in New Zealand’s loose forwards, with Peter Lakai shifting from the openside flank to the now-vacated No.8 jersey to accommodate Segner at No.7. The make-up of the bench has remained the same, with Ethan Blackadder remaining in the No.20 jersey.

Rugby.title: As All Blacks fans ramp up for Rugby's Greatest Rivalry, it would be foolhardy to overlook the NPC
Rugby.summary: While all eyes will inevitably be on South Africa for Rugby's Greatest Rivalry, the NPC will be playing out and it has never been more vital
Rugby.body:
They say, when you meet a new baby in the extended family, it’s poor form to ignore any older siblings in the process of making a spirited dash for the latest arrival. It’s a piece of advice that springs to mind seeing how New Zealand Rugby [NZR] has directed all the media attention at the All Blacks’ tour of South Africa – with the national team jetting off from Auckland on the same day that the National Provincial Championship began.

This is certainly a case of the older sibling being overlooked for the agreeable new arrival, and while there were endless stories and opinion pieces about the All Blacks, there was barely a mention of the fact that Waikato had beaten Bay of Plenty in the opening game of what is now called the Hilux NPC.

Rugby.title: Italy on the hunt for new head coach and WXV training squad named
Rugby.summary: Italy have confirmed the departure of Fabio Roselli as their head coach upon the announcement of a WXV Global Series training squad.
Rugby.body:
Italy have confirmed the departure of Fabio Roselli as the team’s head coach upon the announcement of a WXV Global Series training squad. The training squad will be led by interim head coach Plinio Sciamanna. Italy will play home fixtures against Japan and South Africa in September. In October the Azzurre will play two Tests agains the USA Women’s Eagles in Texas and Tennessee.

Roselli was head coach of Italy for 18 months and saw his team win seven of the 15 matches he presided over. This included Italy’s pool stage exit from Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 after losses to France and South Africa.

Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter has laid down the gauntlet to his internationals to get their fitness up to speed quickly when they return for pre-season training ahead of the new Gallagher PREM season.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter has laid down the gauntlet to his internationals to get their fitness up to speed quickly when they return for pre-season training ahead of the new Gallagher PREM season.

Baxter says that he believes that a good pre-season last summer was one of the reasons the Chiefs took at least a point from every Prem game in the 2025-26 campaign. He says that the Chiefs’ plethora of internationals, who make up the vast majority of the squad, will have to hit the ground running as they look to play catch-up with players who have already been back for a few weeks.

Rugby.summary: The picks will work across five rounds this week, the clubs selecting two players each for their male and female squads.
Rugby.body:
The inaugural season of Ultimate Sevens has seen the first player draft get underway, with 17 nations and 131 players across the men’s and women’s teams set to be allocated. The competition is set for a bumper inaugural season, with fixtures set to take place across four back-to-back weeks in Spain, Wales, France and England in September and head coaches already confirmed.

Each of the six sides are set to feature up to 12 players in both their men’s and women’s squads, comprising two marquee players, nine elite players and one academy player. The picks will work across five rounds this week, the clubs selecting two players each for their male and female squads.

Beauden Barrett has had to be patient waiting for his All Blacks opportunity in 2026, and now that it has finally arrived, he’s cautious not to let the moment overcome him or pass him by.

Rugby.title: Butula reclaim KSSSA Rugby Sevens crown as Kinale Girls make history - the-star.co.ke
Rugby.summary: Butula reclaim KSSSA Rugby Sevens crown as Kinale Girls make history the-star.co.ke
Rugby.body:
Butula Boys Senior School are the new KCB Kenya Secondary Schools Sports Association (KSSSA) Rugby Sevens champions after dismantling Cardinal Otunga Senior School, Mosocho 26-0 in the final played at the MPesa Foundation Academy in Thika, Kiambu County.

The Busia County side reclaimed the title they last won in 2013 with a commanding display on both sides of the ball. Butula made the perfect start as Arthur Amimo crossed for the opening try, with Robert Carlos adding the conversion for a 7-0 lead. Alex Okoth added the second try before Carlos once again converted to hand Butula a comfortable 14-0 advantage at half-time.

Rugby.summary: Corey Kellow isn’t a player who seeks the limelight. The dogged openside flanker, however, has scored a try in his last five NPC games, which places him in rarefied air for champions Canterbury.
Rugby.body:
Corey Kellow isn’t a player who seeks the limelight. The dogged openside flanker, however, has scored a try in his last five NPC games, which places him in rarefied air for champions Canterbury.

With tries in five wins against Bay of Plenty (21-7), Hawke’s Bay (26-7), Manawatu (53-14), Southland (54-14), and Auckland (38-31), Kellow has joined the likes of Randall Scott (1980), Dale Atkins (1986), and Justin Marshall (2001-2002) in scoring tries in five consecutive Division 1 NPC matches for Canterbury. When Canterbury won the title in 2017, the last of their nine-in-10-years sequence, Josh McKay scored tries in six consecutive matches.

Rugby.summary: Title-winning halves Bernard Foley and Nick Phipps are returning to the NSW Waratahs for the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season.
Rugby.body:
Title-winning halves Bernard Foley and Nick Phipps are returning to the NSW Waratahs for the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season, reuniting at the Sydney-based club seven years after they last suited up in cambridge blue together.

Rugby.title: The eternal Wallabies selection conundrum that now falls to Les Kiss
Rugby.summary: There are 18 Test matches between now and the beginning of the 2027 home Rugby World Cup, and the Wallabies must use these games astutely.
Rugby.body:
There are 18 Test matches between now and the beginning of the 2027 home Rugby World Cup, and the Wallabies must use these games astutely. They must be used efficiently to build a Wallabies squad with a genuine depth of 33-40 players, and they must be used accurately to ensure players get the right exposure at the right time.

The first number is 33 because that has been the typical World Cup squad size, and it typically carries around 19-21 forwards with between 12-14 backs. You must also account for injuries, hence the number 40, which is an achievable number but still short of the ‘three-deep in every position’ standard that gets bandied around by rugby pundits.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: Scarlets chief Daniels dismisses Ospreys merger
Rugby.summary: Scarlets managing director Jon Daniels also wants greater transparency from the Welsh Rugby Union as their future hangs in the balance.
Rugby.body:
Scarlets managing director Jon Daniels has called for greater transparency from the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) as their future hangs in the balance. Welsh rugby's governing body has outlined its plans to cut the number of professional teams from four to three by 2028, with Cardiff and Dragons set to be given licences.

That announcement has plunged Scarlets and Ospreys into doubt, with the west licence either being awarded to the Llanelli-based side or their Swansea-based rivals. Daniels dismissed the notion that a merger between the teams - which was close, but ultimately scrapped in 2019 - is a consideration at this stage.

Rugby.body:

The Sharks boss has used Simon Orange’s cheque book to bring in former England stars Courtney Lawes, Joe Marchant, and Welsh duo Tomas Francis and Nicky Smith, who boast almost 300 caps between them, to help him to achieve it.

Rugby.title: 'I’ve been at a fair few clubs – more clubs than Tiger Woods!'
Rugby.summary: Former England U20 international Rory Jennings has called it quits as a professional rugby player, aged 30, after representing 10 different clubs in a nomadic career.
Rugby.body:
Former England U20 international Rory Jennings has called it quits as a professional rugby player, aged 30, after representing 10 different clubs in a nomadic career. Writing on the business social networking site LinkedIn, the fly-half/centre said: “After 12 fantastic years, I’m stepping away from full-time professional rugby and my time with Cardiff Rugby! It’s been an incredible journey—from Bath, Clermont-Auvergne, Newcastle and London Irish through to Cardiff – and I’m deeply grateful for every match, teammate, and lesson along the way.

“I haven’t hung up the boots entirely, though. I’ve joined Rosslyn Park Football Club, which lets me keep scratching that competitive itch on training nights alongside a brilliant group of lads.

Rugby.title: Janse van Rensburg given captaincy ahead of Bok Women's clash with Fiji
Rugby.summary: Libbie Janse van Rensburg will captain South Africa ahead of their second-ever encounter with Fiji this weekend in Suva.
Rugby.body:
Libbie Janse van Rensburg will captain South Africa ahead of their second-ever encounter with Fiji this weekend in Suva. The 31-year-old will become just the 12th player to captain the Springbok Women since their Test debut in 2004 and is the only backline player retained from their last game against the USA Women’s Eagles in mid-July.

In the pack, only Vainah Ubisi and Sizophila Solontsi have retained their starting places from the clash at Loftus Versfeld. Aseza Hele and Lindelwa Gwala will both play for South Africa for the first time since Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025.

Rugby.title: World Rankings: Springboks' place at No.1 under threat in Buenos Aires
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks could go into the four-Test Greatest Rivalry Series as the number one ranked team in the world.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks could go into the four-Test Greatest Rivalry Series (22 August-12 September) as the number one ranked team in the world. South Africa are closing in on an unbroken year-long run at the top, having dethroned the All Blacks last September. But a defeat to Argentina in Buenos Aires this Saturday would result in the All Blacks taking over again.

Rassie Erasmus’ side go into the match at Estadio José Amalfitani with a rankings rating of 93.96, giving them a lead of 1.68 points over the All Blacks, who begin their tour of South Africa against the Stormers in Cape Town on Friday night.

Rugby.summary: Dave Butcher says there “wasn't even a hesitation” when he was asked if he would take up the role as Scotland women’s interim head coach ahead of the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
Dave Butcher says there “wasn’t even a hesitation” when he was asked if he would take up the role as Scotland women’s interim head coach ahead of the WXV Global Series. There is never a dull day in Scottish rugby and, on Monday morning, the governing body announced that head coach Sione Fukofuka was leaving his post after eight months and was returning home to Australia for family and personal reasons.

At that time it was explained that Butcher, who had been an assistant under Fukofuka, was to become interim head coach. Later in the day, Scottish Rugby announced that senior assistant coach Ioan Cunningham was leaving too and that Chris Laidlaw from Harlequins and Tom Luke from Bristol Bears were joining as assistants for the upcoming quintet of Test matches.

Rugby.summary: Wellington have thrown a curveball at old foes Auckland ahead of Saturday's NPC showdown, naming All Black Du'Plessis Kirifi at inside centre.
Rugby.body:
Wellington have thrown a curveball at old foes Auckland ahead of Saturday’s NPC showdown, naming All Black Du’Plessis Kirifi at inside centre. The 29-year-old has 129 first-class games to his name, including eight with the All Blacks, and has never started in any jersey other than the No.7.

Perhaps the most discussed All Blacks omission in 2026, Kirifi started in his familiar openside flanker role in round 1 of the new NPC season last week, with Wellington falling to Hawke’s Bay despite Kirifi’s best efforts. The Hurricanes co-captain won four turnovers and chipped in on attack with 12 carries and a try.

Rugby.title: The ‘big impact’ Will Skelton had on giant Brumbies recruit’s career
Rugby.summary: ACT Brumbies recruit Aiden Stait has opened up on the “big impact” La Rochelle-based Wallaby Will Skelton had on his career.
Rugby.body:
ACT Brumbies recruit Aiden Stait has opened up on the “big impact” La Rochelle-based Wallaby Will Skelton had on his career, having convinced the young lock to initially pursue an opportunity with French club Bayonne.

Stait has returned to Australia after spending a few years in Basque Country with the Top 14 club, having signed a deal with the Brumbies through to the end of 2029. The six-foot-eight second-rower has joined the club ahead of the 2026 Super Rugby AUS campaign.

Rugby.title: All Blacks tour of South Africa is a fact-finding mission for next year
Rugby.summary: I wonder who else remembers that game. You should do, given how much we bang on about the All Blacks’ run of unbeaten games at Eden Park.
Rugby.body:
I wonder who else remembers that game. You should do, given how much we bang on about the All Blacks’ run of unbeaten games at Eden Park. France beat the All Blacks 2-0 in 1994: 22-8 at Lancaster Park and then 23-20 in Auckland. In between, came a loss to the Magpies which is remembered fondly by folk here in Hawke’s Bay, but won’t mean a lot to anyone else.

The “Greatest Rivalry’ tour is about to kick off, apparently. There’s conjecture about who’ll be in the All Blacks team to meet the Stormers in the opening match, debate about the referees appointed for the tests and reminiscences about the last time the team toured South Africa in 1996.

Rugby.title: Wallabies star Rob Valetini reflects on Eddie Jones’ influence
Rugby.summary: This reunion has been a talking point at press conferences this week, with Valetini asked a couple of questions about Jones on Tuesday.
Rugby.body:
Rob Valetini was a trusted member of Eddie Jones’ Wallabies a few years ago, named in the run-on side for every Test during the veteran coach’s second stint with the national team, including four appearances at the 2023 Rugby World Cup.

The Wallabies bowed out of the showpiece event before the quarter-finals for the first time, with defeats to Fiji and Wales seeing them finish third in the group. Jones left Aussie rugby soon after, taking up the head coaching role with Japan.

Rugby.title: Rassie pumps brakes on rugby's attacking trend with World Cup prediction
Rugby.summary: Current projections suggest a high-scoring tournament is coming fans' way, with the recent block of July internationals featuring a jump in the number of tries scored and a slight drop in the influence of set-piece.
Rugby.body:
Rassie Erasmus isn’t so invested in the recent trend of attack-dominated rugby, with the Springboks coach predicting next year’s Rugby World Cup is still likely to feature the same themes that have traditionally dominated its knockout stages.

Erasmus has famously led South Africa to back-to-back World Cup wins since his 2018 appointment as head coach, and will be chasing the first-ever three-peat at next year’s tournament in Australia.

Rugby.title: Siya Kolisi returns to lead much-changed Springbok team in Buenos Aires
Rugby.summary: Rassie Erasmus has made 13 changes to the team that started the 43-0 win over Wales in round three of the Nations Championship in July.
Rugby.body:
Rassie Erasmus has made 13 changes to the team that started the 43-0 win over Wales in round three of the Nations Championship in July for Saturday’s clash with the Pumas at Estadio José Amalfitani in Buenos Aires.

Double World Cup-wining captain Siya Kolisi missed the first three Tests of the year, but is back to lead the team from blindside. The 35-year-old is joined in the starting line-up by other experienced internationals, such as fit-again lock duo, Eben Etzebeth, Lood de Jager, who’ve also been absent in 2026 and bring over 200 caps worth of experience to the team.

Rugby.title: Why £1m-a-season deal will be hard for Pollock and Hearn to find
Rugby.summary: Salary cap regulations might not be high on everyone's holiday reading list, but Eddie Hearn might be interested if he's keen to get Henry Pollock's £1m pay-day.
Rugby.body:
Salary cap regulations might not be high on everyone's holiday reading list, but agent Eddie Hearn might be interested if he's keen to get Henry Pollock's £1m pay-day. The Prem salary cap is currently £6.4m per club. In basic terms, your whole squad's salaries have to add up to £6.4m or less.

There's an outside chance the Northampton back row could get a salary of £1m next season, if a club out there has that amount of space in the cap. The only team thought to be in this bracket, according to the last published salary cap report in 2024-25, would be Newcastle.

Rugby.body:
France full-back Thomas Ramos has agreed to a shock move, swapping Toulouse for Racing 92 when his contract runs out at the end of the season, his current employers have confirmed.

The 52-cap international will move to the French capital after the World Cup in Australia next year, but remaisn committed to Les Rouges et Noir until then. “Thomas Ramos is one of the faces of Stade Toulousain. Beyond his immense talent, he is an exceptional competitor and a player whose high standards elevate the entire team,” said club president, Didier Lacroix.

Rugby.title: Babalwa Latsha talks Boks captaincy and the 'experience of a lifetime'
Rugby.summary: Babalwa Latsha knows the weight and magnitude of being a Springbok captain and she "excitedly" and "humbly" accepted the responsibility when Swys de Bruin named her as the team's new skipper in July.
Rugby.body:
Babalwa Latsha knows the weight and magnitude of being a Springbok captain and she “excitedly” and “humbly” accepted the responsibility when Swys de Bruin named her as the team’s new skipper in July.

Latsha takes over from her close friend Nolusindiso Booi, who she says has helped shape her as a leader. The 32-year-old’s first games in charge as official captain was South Africa’s tied two-Test series against the USA Women’s Eagles.

Rugby.title: McMillan retires from international rugby five months after Scotland recall
Rugby.summary: Louise McMillan has announced her retirement from international rugby five months after her return to the Scotland set-up.
Rugby.body:
Louise McMillan has announced her retirement from international rugby five months after her return to the Scotland set-up. Across a decade long Test career McMillan earned 61 caps, but missed out on a year of international rugby after she was dropped from the Scotland squad ahead of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 by then-head coach Bryan Easson.

Performances for JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby club Saracens, with whom she will continue playing domestic rugby for, earned McMillan a recall and three final caps for her country at this year’s Guinness Women’s Six Nations. Her final cap came in Scotland’s 54-5 loss to Ireland at Dublin’s Aviva Stadium.

Rugby.body:
The four referees for the Greatest Rivalry Series between South Africa and New Zealand have been announced by World Rugby, with Matt Carley taking charge of the first Test at Ellis Park in Johannesburg on 22 August.

Groundbreaking Georgian official Nika Amashukeli has been handed the second Test at the DHL Stadium Cape Town a week later, while Australian official Angus Gardner will run the rule over the third Test, which takes place at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg on 5 September.

Rugby.title: South African rugby 'family secret' adds extra spice to Boks vs All Blacks series
Rugby.summary: Great rivalries need more than close matches. They need inherited grievance, disputed memories and old wounds that can be pressed for fun. They need a little bad blood.
Rugby.body:
Does your family have a secret? A rumour that, if it were true, would shatter relationships? Perhaps an extra-marital affair or a link to organised crime. Maybe your uncle really is a gambling addict. What if your gran really did embezzle from that nursing home?

Best not to think about it. No need to air the dirty laundry. Pour yourself another drink and make small talk with your cousins. Why let the truth get in the way of a good time?

Rugby.body:
Scotland have been able to recall a number of senior forwards upon the announcement of their WXV Global Series squad. Rachel Malcolm, who missed three matches at the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations, returns to the squad as captain. This squad has been named just 24 hours after the bombshell confirmation that Sione Fukofuka has left his post as head coach just shy of eight months in the role. Dave Butcher will lead Scotland as interim head coach.

Rugby.summary: Three-time Super Rugby Aupiki winning head coach Willie Walker has signed on to be head coach of Fiji Women.
Rugby.body:
Three-time Super Rugby Aupiki winning head coach Willie Walker has signed on to be head coach of Fiji Women. Walker has enjoyed established success with the Blues Women in New Zealand since Super Rugby Aupiki’s establishment in 2021, and led them to consecutive titles in 2024, 2025 and 2026.

The 48-year-old concluded his time at the Blues with a win over the NSW Waratahs in a close-fought Super Rugby Champions final in Sydney. Walker said: “It is a privilege to be entrusted with leading the Vodafone Fijiana XV. Fiji has an incredible rugby culture and a talented group of athletes with enormous potential.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu's former coach calls for radical change to tennis which would leave Novak Djokovic very vulnerable
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu's former coach calls for radical change to tennis which would leave Novak Djokovic very vulnerable Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Tennis is one of the most traditional sports there is, but of late changes have been made to try and bring it into the modern world. These have been in an effort to provide a greater fan experience, increase revenue and exposure, and, most importantly, give their star players what they want.

This has resulted in some varied outcomes, most notably with the two-week Masters 1000 events, billed as an effort to reduce the physical strain of such crucial tournaments. This has been a venture not well received.

Tennis.title: World number one Sinner to miss Cincinnati Open
Tennis.summary: World number one Jannik Sinner withdraws from this week's Cincinnati Open because of a knee injury, but still expects to be fit for the US Open later this month.
Tennis.body:
World number one Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from this week's Cincinnati Open because of a knee injury, but still expects to be fit for the US Open later this month. The 24-year-old Italian won his fifth Grand Slam singles title by beating Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final last month, but has not played since.

"After consulting with my doctors and my team, I have to announce that I need to withdraw from the Masters 1000 tournament in Cincinnati," Sinner said. "My right knee has been bothering me and even though we have been working hard with my medical team, I have to accept I'm not ready to compete yet.

The British player left the court in tears after his first match since June, raising concerns about whether his US Open preparations had suffered another major blow.

The 24-year-old was making his comeback in Canada after a recurrence of the bone bruising that had previously kept him sidelined for almost seven months. Draper struggled physically during his match against Terence Atmane and eventually appeared unable to continue at his usual level, but the latest update suggests he will not need another extended absence from competition.

Tennis.title: 114 days and counting
Tennis.summary: BBC Sport analyses Carlos Alcaraz's ongoing absence from tennis and why wrist injuries are so difficult to manage.
Tennis.body:
When Carlos Alcaraz walked off the court at Rod Laver Arena in January, he was on top of the world. At 22, he had just completed the career Grand Slam, beating all-time great Novak Djokovic in the Australian Open final to claim his seventh major title.

A few months earlier he had decimated his rival Jannik Sinner in the US Open final in what was one of most the impressive performances of his illustrious career to date. But the Spaniard has now missed the French Open and Wimbledon, going 114 days without playing a competitive match due to a wrist injury he suffered in April.

Tennis.title: Andy Roddick Delivers Honest Verdict on Emma Raducanu’s US Open Absence: “It Just Stinks”
Tennis.summary: Andy Roddick Delivers Honest Verdict on Emma Raducanu’s US Open Absence: “It Just Stinks” Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu officially pulled out of the US Open on Monday, marking her sixth withdrawal from a major due to physical setbacks in the last five years. This time, it was on account of her stress fracture in her right shin. This drew a sympathetic reaction from former American World No. 1 Andy Roddick, who couldn't help but share his frustration regarding the situation.

"We might not even see her for the rest of this year. It just stinks because she is so good and it's just the stop and start of things," said Roddickon the latest episode of theServed Podcast. "You can't get around a stress fracture, that's not a pain tolerance thing at all. It has to heal otherwise you are going to cause extreme long-term damage. It just stinks. She could be such a bright spot for the tours and it just seems like there are speed bumps all the time, which is just unfortunate."

Tennis.title: What has gone wrong for Jack Draper and Emma Raducanu?
Tennis.summary: What has gone wrong for Jack Draper and Emma Raducanu? The Telegraph
Tennis.body:
Draper’s elbow sounds considerably more complicated. Yes, scans did show bone bruising on the end of his humerus – the big bone that runs from the elbow to the shoulder – when his initial pain was checked out last summer. But he is evidently not receiving such clear diagnoses anymore, because he keeps trying – and failing – to play tournaments. In the last 18 months, he has moved from the acute injury phase to something more chronic.

In that same Sky Sports interview in Montreal, Draper explained that “it’s important for people to recognise that the injury I have is very complex, it’s very complicated and everyone around me is doing everything we can to help this keep moving along”.

Tennis.title: Carlos Alcaraz, Jack Draper In Doubt For US Open As Sinner Reportedly Undergoes Medical Check
Tennis.summary: Carlos Alcaraz, Jack Draper In Doubt For US Open As Sinner Reportedly Undergoes Medical Check ubitennis.net
Tennis.body:
Fresh doubts have been raised over Carlos Alcaraz’s chances of defending his title at the US Open after he withdrew from a key warm-up event. The world No. 2 has withdrawn from the Cincinnati Masters, which was set to be his first event on the Tour since April. Alcaraz has been sidelined with a wrist injury. He is understood to be dealing with wrist tenosynovitis, a condition where inflammation occurs in the protective sheath surrounding the wrist tendons.

“We know Carlos is doing everything he can to get back to playing tournaments as soon as possible,’ tournament director Bob Moran said in a press release. “We wish him the best with his recovery and look forward to welcoming him back to Cincinnati in the future.”

Tennis.title: Jack Draper in tears amid injury concern during defeat to Terence Atmane on return to action in Montreal
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper in tears amid injury concern during defeat to Terence Atmane on return to action in Montreal Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper was left in tears after losing to Terence Atmane as the Brit's long-term arm injury appeared to resurface and hamper him on his return to action at the Canadian Open.

Playing in just his sixth tournament of the year, and a first since pulling out of Wimbledon, Draper was beaten 6-3 2-6 6-2 by France's Atmane. After a rusty start, Draper appeared to have found form as he dominated the second set, but his performance suddenly dropped off in the decider as the power in his serves and groundstrokes reduced massively.

Tennis.body:
Carlos Alcaraz has withdrawn from the Cincinnati Open as he continues to recover from a wrist injury. The world number two has not played since he pulled out of the Barcelona Open in April, missing Wimbledon and the chance to defend his French Open title.

After winning the event in 2025, Spain's Alcaraz was due to return at the Cincinnati Open as part of preparations for his defence of the US Open, which begins on 30 August. Instead, the organisers of the Ohio event - which starts on 11 August - said that "an ongoing wrist injury" will prevent the 23-year-old from taking part.

Tennis.summary: Tearful Jack Draper loses on comeback from injury at Canadian Open The Guardian
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper was in tears during a first-round comeback defeat by Térence Atmane at the Canadian Open. The Briton was competing for the first time since pulling out of Wimbledon with a recurrence of a bruised bone in his left arm, and was beaten 6-3, 2-6, 6-2 in Montreal.

The 24-year-old was visibly upset during a changeover in the third set. His serve speed had significantly dropped, and he appeared concerned about his left arm. He has a wildcard entry for the Cincinnati Open, beginning next week, but there will be doubts about his involvement after this defeat, as well as regarding his fitness for the US Open.

Tennis.body:
Once Emma Raducanu had the temerity to win the US Open and thrust herself into the spotlight, it did not take long for her to become a punchbag for armchair sports fans in Britain.

No athlete who is injury prone needs reminding they are injury prone, but in Raducanu’s case there is a gleeful pile-on to ensure she is endlessly aware. The 23-year-old should even just retire, according to some experts in basements, because she would clearly rather pursue various business ventures than focus on tennis.

Tennis.body:
As the umpire called the winning point, Alexandra Eala collapsed to the ground in tears - knowing her country had been with her for every step of the tournament. She overcame weather delays, and the loss of the first set, to defeat world number three Jessica Pegula in the Washington Open final, becoming the first Filipina to win a WTA title.

"To the Filipino community, here in DC and back home, wherever you are in the world. I really feel all the love." Even Pegula was impressed by the turnout on Monday, for the continuation of Sunday's final.

“She has really had a lot of bad luck with injuries throughout her career. We must not forget that she had wrist surgery, she had foot problems, and now she has to deal with this stress fracture.”

Golf.summary: Wildcreek Golf Course, the new host of the World Long Drive Championship, is a remade Reno muni that doubles as the home of the First Tee. The post This new-look muni is readying to host the game’s longest drivers appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
After several years in the wilderness, the World Long Drive Championship has found a new home in Reno, Nev. The longer version involves the property that will host the event, a municipal facility whose evolution reflects the changing face of Reno golf itself.

Wildcreek Golf Course opened in 1978, at a time when Reno needed all the golf it could get. In those days, tour buses streamed over the Sierra from California, carrying throngs of visitors keen to hit the tables and the tee. Reno had casinos in abundance but was relatively shy on courses.

Golf.title: The U.S Amateur's most important lesson comes from ... an accounting professor?
Golf.summary: When Brett Patterson qualified for the U.S. Open at 19, he thought golf was his future. Now he's back in the fray with a different lesson in hand. The post The U.S Amateur’s most important lesson comes from … an accounting professor? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — The U.S. Amateur Championship is a proving ground filled with lessons for golf’s youngest stars. But at this year’s edition at Merion East, one important lesson will come not from the Hugh Wilson design on the outskirts of Philadelphia, but from a 34-year-old accounting professor competing for the title.

One whose journey to the U.S. Am is different than most. Fifteen years ago, Brett Patterson was an ascending collegiate talent as a freshman at Middle Tennessee State University. At 19 years old, Patterson fired a second-round 62 at Hawks Ridge Golf Club in final U.S. Open qualifying to punch his ticket to the 2011 U.S. Open. Rory McIlroy romped to his first major title that week while Patterson shot 77-78 to miss the cut at Congressional.

Golf.title: Jon Rahm just added to his LIV Golf fortune – but he’s still reportedly owed millions
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm just added to his LIV Golf fortune – but he’s still reportedly owed millions Golfmagic
Golf.body:
Jon Rahm has taken his LIV Golf earnings beyond $90 million after securing a third consecutive Individual Championship at the weekend. The Spaniard finished T41 at Trump National Bedminster – his worst result since joining LIV Golf – but had already built such a commanding lead in the season-long standings that his nearest pursuer Bryson DeChambeau could not catch him.

With just one regular-season event remaining in Indianapolis, Rahm has therefore secured another individual title without needing to wait for the final tournament. The Individual Championship bonus may have dropped this season from $18 million to $6 million, but Rahm's latest success still provides him with a significant financial boost.

It was an action-packed week at Bedminster, where trophies were awarded, and the history books were rewritten. Here’s a look back at the best moments. Jon Rahm clinched another season-long Individual Championship and Joaquin Niemann added to his record number of tournament wins on a day that reflected their success on LIV Golf. Rahm won his third consecutive season-long title — 2024, 2025, 2026 — while Crushers GC claimed the team title Sunday at LIV Golf New York. Niemann, meanwhile, fought off Harold Varner III to win his ninth career individual tournament title, extending his all-time record, and his second win of the season.

Crushers GC's win in Bedminster was also their 11th regular-season team title in LIV Golf, extending their own all-time record as the winningest team in league history. Here is a last look at some of the most notable performances from LIV Golf New York.

I wasn’t living in my home state in 2021 when I would have had an opportunity to qualify for the Pennsylvania Amateur at Merion. Suffice to say, the chances kept eluding me. But last month, ahead of this week’s U.S. Amateur, the stars finally aligned for me to play the most famous course in Philly.

Golf.title: What is Bryson DeChambeau talking about now?
Golf.summary: What is Bryson DeChambeau talking about now? Golfshake.com
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau has always divided opinion. A bit like Patrick Reed, he is a Marmite golfer - you either love him or you hate him. You never quite know what you are going to get with him, whether it is his thrilling attacking play and monstrous drives or the rounds where he spends 18 holes up to his neck in thick rough. And he is never far away from controversy, such as the two-stroke penalty he suffered at The Open Championship for improving his lie.

In an exclusive with the New York Post, DeChambeau says he wants to see LIV Golf teams own "stadium" home courses and also wants to have the ability to play on the PGA Tour in addition to LIV.

Golf.title: Inside LIV Golf's wild week: Bryson, Trump and the mystery investor surfaces
Golf.summary: A frenetic week for LIV Golf at Trump Bedminster ended with appearances by President Trump and a representative from LIV's reported investor. The post Inside LIV Golf’s wild week: Bryson, Trump and the mystery investor surfaces appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
BEDMINSTER, N.J. — As LIV Golf CEO Scott O’Neil walked the final few holes with the last group on a sweltering Sunday at Trump Bedminster, he had an inside-the-ropes special guest at his side: Ted Goldthorpe, the head of BC Partners Credit, which manages more than $10 billion globally across more than 300 investments. One of the latest companies Goldthorpe’s team reportedly has been kicking the tires on: yep, LIV Golf, which on Wednesday announced it had come to terms with an unnamed investor that will “carry and fund” the beleaguered league into 2027 and beyond.

LIV has not officially acknowledged BC Partners as its would-be funder, or lender. That news came to light via Bloomberg and the Financial Times, the latter of which reported that the deal will be consummated only if BC Partners and other possible investors receive assurances that enough of LIV’s A-listers will hang around beyond this season. Adding intrigue to the dealmaking is the fact that BC Partners is a lender to GSE Worldwide, the sports and entertainment marketing agency that represents LIV’s biggest star, Bryson DeChambeau, along with Joaquin Niemann, the 27-year-old Chilean who won his ninth LIV title here Sunday, with a three-shot win over Harold Varner. GSE said in a statement earlier this week that it had no involvement with BC Partners’ “potential financing transaction involving LIV Golf,” nor, the agency said, was it aware of any discussions happening between the two parties.

Golf.title: Michael Brennan's clubs: What's the deal with his mysterious Titleist proto 3-wood?

Golf.body:
Michael Brennan is once again a winner on the PGA Tour, earning his second PGA Tour victory and punching his ticket to the FedEx Cup playoffs at the Wyndham Championship. Brennan collected his second victory in the last three weeks for Titleist’s mysterious GTS prototype 3-wood. The 24-year-old was actually the first player to be spotted with the unknown GTS fairway wood option at the Texas Children’s Houston Open during the GTS driver launch, but didn’t game the prototype until two months later at the Charles Schwab Challenge.

Titleist has thus far not commented on the prototype, but we can speculate that the GTS may have similar characteristics to the GT1 3Tour fairway wood that both Brennan and Cameron Young — who switched to the prototype this week — previously played.

Golf.title: Michael Block walks off course at senior event, is DQ'd
Golf.summary: Michael Block received one of the strangest DQs of the 2026 golf season on Sunday, and neither side seems entirely sure why. The post Michael Block walks off course at senior event, is DQ’d appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
It’s the senior tour DQ heard ’round the world, if such a thing exists. Michael Block’s disqualification from the Staysure PGA Seniors Championship in Aberdeen, Scotland was not just shocking because it was, well, a story of a DQ from a Legends Tour event. It was shocking because it arrived with a torrent of criticism, a two-shot penalty for showing up late to the tee box, a series of competing accusations … and a much, much larger dose of confusion.

So, what exactly happened? Let’s recount the facts. Things were not going well for Michael Block, senior golf sensation, at the Staysure PGA Seniors Championship. He’d posted three consecutive over-par scores at Trump International — 76-73-78 — leading into Sunday’s final round, an 11-over score that would have been good for 49th place in the competition.

Golf.title: Why men should pay attention to Asterisk Talley's winning U.S. Women's Am clubs
Golf.summary: Asterisk Talley won the 2026 U.S. Women's Amateur. How she builds the bag can teach the weekend warrior a few lessons. The post Why men should pay attention to Asterisk Talley’s winning U.S. Women’s Am clubs appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Seventeen-year-old Asterisk Talley took home the trophy at this year’s U.S. Women’s Amateur at The Honors course. After multiple delays due to storms, the final match came down to Talley and No.1 seed 17-year-old Anna Iwanaga. Talley ended up victorious, winning 8&6 over Iwanaga in the 36-hole final match with nine birdies and an eagle. If you listen to our Fully Equipped Podcast, you’ll often hear us say that the women’s game has more relatable equipment to the average golfer, so let’s see what we can learn from Talley’s winning TaylorMade setup.

The good news for the guys? This is probably one of the more “crafty” women’s setups I’ve seen. It’s a fun bag. Yup. Jumbo. On all her clubs. I had a chance to hang out with Asterisk for a little bit on the range at Whirlwind Golf Club earlier this year, and it was the first thing I noticed too. I asked her about it, and she had a pretty simple answer for me.
