Golf.title: Asterisk Talley's U.S. Women's Amateur win delivered the message she'd been sending
Golf.summary: Asterisk Talley's dominant U.S. Women's Amateur win was years in the making. Afterward, the message she'd been sending was finally received. The post Asterisk Talley’s U.S. Women’s Amateur win delivered the message she’d been sending appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Four months ago, Asterisk Talley stood on the 12th tee at Augusta National with seven holes between her and the Augusta National Women’s Amateur title. The 17-year-old had just made her first bogey of the week at the 11th but was still in command of the tournament.

Twenty minutes later, Asterisk Talley had lost the tournament after a quadruple bogey that saw her put two balls in the water from the back bunker. After limping home with tears in her eyes, Asterisk Talley stood at the mic and showed grace as she answered questions about a brutal life lesson delivered in public. A month later at the Chevron Championship, Asterisk Talley explained that while those scars were painful, she realized they were the price of wanting to be great. That you can’t win unless you’re willing to risk being broken.

Golf.title: Michael Brennan's Wyndham win ended with touching reminder from his mom
Golf.summary: Michael Brennan won the Wyndham to make the playoffs. After his win, his mom reminded him of something else that came with his win. The post Michael Brennan’s Wyndham win ended with touching reminder from his mom appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Michael Brennan didn’t want to be done playing golf. The 24-year-old had been in contention the past two Sundays and entered the Wyndham Championship feeling like his game was finally where it needed to be. There was only one problem. After struggling for most of the year, Brennan entered the PGA Tour’s regular-season finale ranked 105th in the FedEx Cup Playoff standings. He needed a three-way tie for second or better at Sedgefield Country Club to keep his season going to Memphis.

Brennan opened with rounds of 66 and 65 to enter the weekend three shots off the pace set by Beau Hossler. A sizzling Saturday 63 pulled Brennan even with Hossler and then he put his foot on the gas on Sunday, reeling off five straight birdies on the front nine to take the lead and put the pressure on Hossler, who needed a win to keep his season alive, to catch him down the stretch.

Golf.title: Brooks Koepka offers unflinching assessment of PGA Tour season: 'Pathetic'
Golf.summary: After missing out on his final chance to make next week's FedEx Cup playoffs, Brooks Koepka offered a searing assessment of his season. The post Brooks Koepka offers unflinching assessment of PGA Tour season: ‘Pathetic’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Heading into the final regular-season event of the PGA Tour season, Brooks Koepka needed to conjure some magic. The five-time major winner left LIV and rejoined the PGA Tour in January, and the expectation was that the 36-year-old would pick up right where he left off, given the eight wins he had accumulated between 2015 and 2021. (Koepka won his 9th PGA Tour event and fifth major, the 2023 PGA Championship, while playing as a member of LIV Golf.)

But Koepka’s Tour re-entry didn’t produce the level of performance he was hoping for — at least relatively speaking. He made 10 of 15 cuts with six top-25 finishes, but never really contended for a title.

Before longtime CBS broadcaster Andrew Catalon starting calling golf tournaments, he realized the core CBS golf broadcast team was something special. On this week’s episode of Subpar, Catalon, who also works NFL and college basketball games for CBS, explained how he started calling golf tournaments — and what it was like to invited to join CBS’ Masters broadcast team.

“I did the digital, featured group and that type, for 10 years,” Catalon told hosts Colt Knost and Drew Stoltz. “My first one was [Charl] Schwartzel [in 2011]. And then 2020 with Covid, I did it from my basement and that was my last one, digital. 2021 was my first one on the main broadcast.

Golf.title: Niemann, Varner III and Westwood share LIV Golf New York going into last day
Golf.summary: Niemann, Varner III and Westwood share LIV Golf New York going into last day Arab News PK
Golf.body:
BEDMINSTER: Joaquin Niemann’s dominant week hit its first speed bump, but he remains well positioned to secure his second LIV Golf title of the season. The LIV Golf New York 2026 36-hole leader opened Saturday with a double bogey on the par-4 first, the first blemish on his card all week, but he battled back throughout the day en route to a 1-under 70. He heads into the final round at 14-under, maintaining the outright lead at Trump National Golf Club Bedminster.

Niemann admitted the start stung but said he was able to reset quickly. “Obviously not the best tee shot coming out to start the round, but it was kind of good to just be back into that moment,” Niemann said. “It was a little bit frustrating. I think I was able to handle it pretty good.”

A young girl, no older than two, had stepped over the ropeline and into the field of play, prancing through the grass in the direction of Hossler.

Golf.title: He faked a hole in one. Now he’s paying for it
Golf.summary: After a wild cheating scandal unfolded at WingHaven Country Club near St. Louis, the golfer at the center of it confessed and offered a plea. The post He faked a hole in one. Now he’s paying for it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Being labeled a cheater on the golf course is a black mark that’s virtually impossible to remove. Whether it’s a wild cheating scandal at Q School or someone fluffing their lie during a Saturday morning scramble, cheating in golf isn’t new.

But what happened recently at WingHaven Country Club near St. Louis rocked the local golf scene and is spreading after the culprit went on ESPN Radio in St. Louis to confess. To set the scene, the events happened during a member-member championship at WingHaven last weekend. The golfer in question, who we won’t name to avoid piling on, is a plus-2 handicap and played college golf at a junior college before having what he described to ESPN as “a cup of coffee” at Eastern Illinois University.

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau wants to play LIV and PGA Tour. But 'no merger' is on horizon
Golf.summary: While Bryson DeChambeau hopes to one day play on both LIV Golf and the PGA Tour, CEO Brian Rolapp said "no merger" has been discussed. The post Bryson DeChambeau wants to play LIV and PGA Tour. But ‘no merger’ is on horizon appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau is “100 percent” confident in LIV Golf’s future after CEO Scott O’Neil announced earlier this week that the league had found a “lead investor” to keep it alive past 2026. But DeChambeau told The New York Post that his bigger goal is not just to grow the rebel league but to get to a place where he can play in both LIV and the PGA Tour simultaneously.

“One hundred percent, no question. As long as the good of the game stays in view going forward, I totally think we can get there,” DeChambeau told Mark Cannizzaro at LIV Golf New York on Thursday when asked if he felt LIV’s future was secure.

Hossler is one of many players in the field who need a win to keep their season going through August.

Golf.title: Want to hit a proper pitch? Master this 1 key
Golf.summary: Top 100 Teacher Krista Dunton explains why getting too steep can cause pitching problems — and how to avoid it. The post Want to hit a proper pitch? Master this 1 key appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One key to hitting a great pitch shot is balancing steep angles in the setup with shallow angles during the motion. If you get too steep in the swing, the leading edge can dig and create inconsistent contact. Here’s how to keep that from happening.

At address, keep your hands neutral with minimal shaft lean, while your head and chest are slightly ahead of the ball. With this setup, you’ll create the necessary steepness in the body to hit a proper pitch. Now, for the shallow motion. Set the clubface open at address and un-cock your wrists.

Golf.title: Can't find a hat without a logo? Blame a refrigerator salesman
Golf.summary: How do today's pros command seven figures for a hat sponsorship? It all started at the 1968 PGA Championship ... with a refrigerator salesman. The post Can’t find a hat without a logo? Blame a refrigerator salesman appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
As with most things modern in golf, Arnold Palmer played a part in the evolution of golf headwear. His win at the 1954 U.S. Amateur wasn’t just the King’s first step to the throne; photographs from his quarterfinal win are among the earliest of an elite golfer wearing a ball cap.

Flip your lid a decade-plus later: Another King — Lou, senior vice president of marketing at Amana Refrigeration — is watching Julius Boros outduel Arnie to victory at the 1968 PGA Championship in Texas. History has it that at one point in the television broadcast, Boros pulled an Amana-branded promotional hat from his golf bag to protect against the blazing San Antonio sun.

Golf.title: Brad Faxon recalls his wild ride at the '85 Honda Classic — with Michael Bamberger on the bag
Golf.summary: In 1985, Brad Faxon hired Michael Bamberger to caddie for him at the Honda Classic — and the experience made a lasting impact. The post Brad Faxon recalls his wild ride at the ’85 Honda Classic — with Michael Bamberger on the bag appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In 1985, second-year pro Brad Faxon and aspiring writer Michael Bamberger were two kids trying to figure it out. Faxon was in search of his game, Bamberger in search of a gig. Here the golfer-coach-broadcaster recalls their wild ride at the ’85 Honda Classic, where one of them passed go and the other — well, Faxon tells the rest.

On a late-fall day in 1984, after my rookie season on the PGA Tour had wrapped up, a personal letter arrived at my new townhouse in Orlando. Personal letters had a lot of impact in those days, and this one landed with a particular thud. It was written on a manual type-writer and, though the tone was modest, it went on for pages. The author told me about his own play as a bogey golfer, his experience as an occasional caddie while in high school and his first postcollege job as a reporter at a weekly newspaper on Martha’s Vineyard, an island off Cape Cod in Massachusetts. Eventually, he made his pitch: Was I looking for a caddie for the 1985 golf season, and, if so, could he throw his hat in the ring?

Golf.title: U.S. Women’s Amateur weathers third suspension in 3 days
Golf.summary: Severe weather suspended Round of 16 play at the 2026 U.S. Women’s Amateur. The matches are set to resume Saturday morning. The post U.S. Women’s Amateur weathers third suspension in 3 days appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
OLTEWAH, Tenn. — For the third straight day, Mother Nature showed no mercy at the U.S. Women’s Amateur. Just as was the case on Wednesday and Thursday here at the Honors Course, wild weather conditions halted play Friday afternoon with all eight Round of 16 matches underway. Unlike the first two days, though, on Friday play never resumed.

After nearly three hours of rain and repeated lightning flashes, the USGA suspended the matches for the remainder of the day, citing unsafe conditions. Play is expected to resume Saturday at 7 a.m. ET.

Golf.title: Rachel Heck finds something she's been missing: 'I haven't felt that in a long time'
Golf.summary: For Rachel Heck, Thursday’s 1-up victory over Anna Davis at the 2026 U.S. Women’s Amateur was about more than advancing to the next round. The post Rachel Heck finds something she’s been missing: ‘I haven’t felt that in a long time’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
OLTEWAH, Tenn. – For Rachel Heck, Thursday’s 1-up victory over Anna Davis at the 2026 U.S. Women’s Amateur was about more than advancing to the next round. This week marks Heck’s third competitive event of the year, but it wasn’t until her match against Davis, the 2022 Augusta National Women’s Amateur champion — which came down to the final hole — that she felt something she’d been missing for a long time.

“So much excitement,” Heck said after winning her match, “It was so fun to feel those emotions again, the adrenaline and the nerves. I haven’t felt that in a long time.” The win marked Heck’s first match-play victory at the U.S. Women’s Amateur since her quarterfinal run in 2023, a meaningful milestone as she makes her return to competitive golf.

Golf.title: The hidden value of playing golf with a pro can endure for decades
Golf.summary: Pro-ams give the duffing class an inside-the-ropes illusion that we play the same game the pros play. But there's another benefit, too. The post The hidden value of playing golf with a pro can endure for decades appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Baseball has fantasy camps but golf has something far better: the pro-am. Pro-ams give the duffing class an inside-the-ropes illusion that we play the same game the pros play. Which we do, in a limited way. Pros like to moan about the hardship of playing with us. Male pros in their golfing prime, I should say — PGA Tour stars and the like. LPGA pros have always had a better attitude about their pro-am obligations. The women seem to understand, maybe on instinct alone, that ams pay bills, and the pro-am itself connects amateur fans to their assigned pros forever.

In the early 1980s, I caddied in an LPGA pro-am on Long Island with Lori Garbacz as the headliner. She was personality-plus. I followed her in the agate type of various newspapers and magazines for the rest of her long career, and laughed out loud when I read that she had instructed her caddie to order a Domino’s pizza for on-course delivery during a crawling U.S. Open round at Colonial Country Club. So on brand, based on my half-day with Lori G. As a marketing tool, you can’t beat the pro-am. It comes right out of the long, rich history of human intercourse. People needing people, etc.

Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau was caught throwing a tantrum on the 5th tee box after a nightmare opening to the first round of LIV Golf New York at Trump National Bedminster. The Crushers GC captain endured one of his worst starts of the season, slipping to 4-over par through his opening four holes after a disastrous run that included a double bogey at the 1st, another bogey at the 2nd and a further dropped shot on the 4th.

Clearly unhappy with his rough start, DeChambeau took a swig from a plastic bottle before walking towards the bin on the 5th tee. In a visible display of frustration, the 32-year-old American aggressively threw his bottle at the bin, only to miss completely as it bounced off the rim and onto the grass.

Golf.title: How a signed Nelly Korda glove became a treasured gift to kids half a world away
Golf.summary: An autographed Nelly Korda golf glove made its way to a junior golf program in Brazil. But it wouldn't have happened without some help. The post How a signed Nelly Korda glove became a treasured gift to kids half a world away appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Nelly Korda’s autograph is as distinctive as her swing. She signs her first name only, with a towering “N” followed by wavy letters that could almost pass for markings on a polygraph. Like most of her peers on the LPGA Tour, Korda is generous with her John Hancock. After any given round, the number of signatures she doles out is apt to exceed the score on her card.

Fans approach her with all kinds of items: flags, programs, caps, shirts. With a few pen strokes, ordinary objects become memorabilia. Some are retained as treasured keepsakes. Others turn up on eBay. Still others make their way to places their original owners could never have imagined. Each becomes part of a story.

Golf.summary: After 36 holes of stroke play at the 2026 U.S. Women's Amateur, a nine-player playoff was needed to decide the final spots. The post 2026 U.S. Women’s Amateur: Marathon 9-player playoff decides final 64 appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
OOLTEWAH, Tenn. – After two rounds of stroke play at the 2026 U.S. Women’s Amateur, two players sit atop the leaderboard. Anna Iwanaga, a 17-year-old from Japan, held onto her first-round lead to earn co-medalist honors, at six under, alongside 15-year-old Hailey Kim of Simi Valley, Calif.

Just one stroke behind the co-medalists was 17-year-old Asterisk Talley, whose second-round 3-under 69 secured her the No. 3 seed entering match play. The players battled more than just one another. A weather delay of nearly two and a half hours suspended second-round play on Wednesday and forced competitors to return the following day to complete their rounds.After regular play concluded, nine players were tied at five over, with just two spots remaining in the 64-player match play field: Bridget Boczar, Paula Francisco, Sarah Lydic, Claire Swathwood, Eliana Saga, Kathryn VanArragon, Nobelle Park, Addison Klonowski and Hsin Chun Liao.

Golf.title: In PGA Tour schedule shakeup, a playoff host won’t be in Championship Series
Golf.summary: Memphis, which has hosted a PGA Tour playoff event since 2022, won’t stage a PGA Tour Championship Series tournament. The post In PGA Tour schedule shakeup, a playoff host won’t be in Championship Series appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Memphis has hosted PGA Tour tournaments since 1958 and a Tour playoff event since 2022, but the city will not be part of the Tour’s top-level circuit slated to start in 2028. The schedule shakeup, first reported by the Memphis Commercial Appeal, was confirmed in statements given to GOLF.com by the Tour and FedEx, a longtime Tour sponsor and whose name is attached to the current Memphis event, the FedEx St. Jude Championship. That tournament will be played next week at TPC Southwind and next year as well, but then no more in its current role.

The news comes two months after the Tour announced it would be creating a Championship Series, featuring 23 to 24 events and its highest-rated players, and a lower-tier Challenger Series starting in 2028. The Tour’s sponsorship deal with FedEx — which includes the backing of the Memphis event and the Tour’s seasonlong points race and postseason — is set to end at the end of next year.

Golf.body:

Golf.title: Ryder Cup stars join Irish Open field
Golf.summary: Robert MacIntyre, Patrick Reed, Francesco Molinari and Sepp Straka will play the Irish Open at the Trump International Golf Links & Hotel in Doonbeg, County Clare from 9-13 September.
Golf.body:
Robert MacIntyre, Patrick Reed, Francesco Molinari and Sepp Straka will play the Irish Open at the Trump International Golf Links & Hotel in Doonbeg from 9-13 September. Defending champion Rory McIlroy and two-time major winner John Rahm are the headline attractions in a field that also contains home favourites Shane Lowry and Padraig Harrington, as well as Luke Donald, Tyrrell Hatton, and the Hojgaard brothers, Rasmus and Nicolai.

American Reed, who won the Masters in 2018, currently leads the Race to Dubai and has won twice on the DP World Tour this year. The 36-year-old announced his departure from LIV Golf in January and is eligible to return to the PGA Tour this month.

Golf.body:
Round one of the 2026 U.S. Women’s Amateur is complete, and the Honors Course wasted no time showing its teeth. Pete Dye’s championship layout demanded precision from start to finish, challenging players with exacting tee shots, uneven lies in the fairway, and lightning-fast greens that were unrelenting.

Leading the pack was 17-year-old Anna Iwanaga, who shot an impressive five-under 67 to give her a two-shot advantage on the field heading into the second round. Just two shots behind her were Madison Dabagia and Jie-En Lin, who shared second place at three-under after steady opening rounds.

Golf.title: Tour Validated: Launch-monitor numbers are important — but focus on this too
Golf.summary: Johnny Wunder sits down with Marshall Thompson from Fujikura to walk through why Ventus has continued to dominate the PGA Tour and more. The post Tour Validated: Launch-monitor numbers are important — but focus on this too appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Every few weeks, golf equipment content focuses heavily on launch-monitor numbers: high launch, low spin, smash factor, ball speed. It dominates digital feeds, making for clean, digestible metrics.

However, in a tour truck on a random Tuesday morning at a PGA Tour event, the conversation sounds completely different. I have yet to hear a player walk on a truck and say “I wanna hit it farther.” The best players and fitters in the world don’t look at equipment that way — the priority is reliability.

Golf.title: LIV says it has found investor to keep league alive
Golf.summary: LIV Golf has found a "lead" investor, according to CEO Scott O'Neil, that will keep the league afloat under a new structure. The post LIV says it has found investor to keep league alive appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
After months of deliberation about the future of LIV Golf, the league has apparently solved part of its dilemma. It has a new “lead” investor lined up, according to a statement from LIV CEO Scott O’Neil, who was set to meet with reporters Wednesday morning at LIV’s event in New Jersey.

According to O’Neil, an agreement is in place with the unnamed investor and comes alongside “strong interest” from various parties for potential minority investments. The deal has been approved by LIV’s board and is expected to reach final terms next month. No financial terms were announced by the league, though the announcement comes just days after reports that LIV was closing in on a $250 million investment.

Golf.title: 'Where everyone would want to be': Major champ eyes PGA Tour return if LIV folds
Golf.summary: Major champion Cameron Smith admitted on Tuesday that if LIV Golf does not survive the year, he would pursue a PGA Tour return. The post ‘Where everyone would want to be’: Major champ eyes PGA Tour return if LIV folds appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Cameron Smith’s move to LIV Golf, as the PGA Tour’s reigning Players champion no less, was one of the most shocking developments in pro golf’s lengthy saga. Fast-forward four years, and Smith may be looking to reverse the decision.

Ahead of a players-only meeting at this week’s LIV Golf New York event at Trump Bedminster, Smith and his LIV teammates sat down for a press conference. When pressed about LIV Golf’s increasingly dire future, Smith admitted that should the upstart league disappear after this season, he’d be prepared “to go back to old times” and rejoin the PGA Tour.

Uncertainty over LIV's final tournament of the season, which takes place on August 27-30 in Michigan, has lingered, major winner Martin Kaymer previously suggesting that he did not think the event would occur, giving it just a five per cent chance of happening.

The creation of LIV Golf sent shockwaves through the golfing world following its inception in 2021, where it was positioned as a rival to the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. LIV is now bidding to seek alternative investment.

Golf.title: LIV players discussed their future for 90 minutes. But said little about it
Golf.summary: LIV players met at Trump Bedminster to discuss the league’s next steps. But they largely declined to share what those steps might be. The post LIV players discussed their future for 90 minutes. But said little about it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
BEDMINSTER, N.J. — It’s fitting that the setting for LIV’s latest players’ meeting was at President Trump’s club here in New Jersey’s rolling horse country, because the convene had all the secrecy of a sealed-door session in the White House Situation Room.

Golf.title: Cam Smith wants LIV Golf to live on but ‘100%’ would return to PGA Tour
Golf.summary: Cam Smith wants LIV Golf to live on but ‘100%’ would return to PGA Tour The Guardian
Golf.body:
Cameron Smith wants LIV Golf to survive but if it doesn’t, he would “100%” return to the PGA Tour. “I mean, if it was the only option, I think that’s where everyone would want to be for sure, 100%,” the Australian former world No 2 said ahead of this week’s LIV Golf New York event. “It would go back to old times.”

But Smith made it clear he would strongly prefer that the current times with LIV Golf can continue. “I want it to work, really, to be honest. It’s great fun out here. The team that we’ve got, I feel like we make each other better, better people and better golfers as well,” Smith said. “Yeah, I’d hate to see it go away. We’ll see what happens.”

Golf.title: Fix this common flaw to stabilize the clubface and improve contact
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tony Ruggiero shares how you can keep from stalling near contact and hit more crisp iron shots. The post Fix this common flaw to stabilize the clubface and improve contact appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I, along with my good friend and fellow GOLF Top 100 Teacher Wayne Flint, have been working with Buddy Hansen, one of the better amateurs in the Philadelphia area, on a swing fault we see at every level of the game. As Buddy approached impact, his chest would stall. When that happens, the hands and arms have to take over the release. This is no good because any release pattern that relies on hand timing instead of proper body sequencing is going to be less reliable and predictable.

For Buddy, it showed up most in his iron play. He simply wasn’t striking the ball as solidly as he wanted. He could hit a great shot, but the misses were inconsistent. His swing didn’t need a rebuild, it just needed a tune-up in one specific area.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: Is it legal to touch your intended line to remove loose impediments?
Golf.summary: Is it permissible to touch your intended line on the green in order to remove loose impediments? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: Is it legal to touch your intended line to remove loose impediments? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. At this year’s Players Championship, Xander Schauffele’s caddie appeared to touch the green on Xander’s line while picking up a loose impediment. What is the rule? —Jim Kelly, Lewisville, NC

Rules 8.2b and 8.1a(2) both mention in that you can’t (a) alter conditions to effect where the ball may go after the next stroke, or (b) move loose impediments to improve the line of play, which seems to restrict the amount of moving of loose impediments you can do. In a scenario where someone wants to putt from a long distance off a green, can they remove all loose impediments along the line all the way to the hole? —Mark McBride, via email

Golf.title: Team Power Rankings: LIV Golf New York
Golf.summary: Team Power Rankings: LIV Golf New York LIV Golf
Golf.body:
Captain Jon Rahm leads Legion XIII into Trump National Golf Club Bedminster, which might prove to be one of the season’s toughest tests. As LIV Golf heads to Trump National Golf Club Bedminster for LIV Golf New York, the stage is set for the 11th stop on the 2026 schedule. It's been nearly three years since the league's last visit to Bedminster, and 33 players from that 2023 field return to a course that has only gotten tougher. The total yardage has been stretched by more than 125 yards, with new back tees adding length to the ninth, 13th and 16th holes.

Trump National Bedminster opened in 2004 under the design of Tom Fazio and has been ranked among the top 100 courses in America by Golf magazine. At 7,651 yards and playing to a par of 71, it's the second-longest course the league has played this season, trailing only Trump National Washington D.C. The course previously hosted LIV Golf events in 2022 and 2023, with Henrik Stenson and 4Aces GC taking the individual and team titles in the first year, and Cameron Smith and Ripper GC sweeping both trophies in the second.

Badminton.title: 'Uniquely Indian': PV Sindhu praises langur mimicry atrists depolyes to keep monkeys away at BWF World Championships
Badminton.summary: 'Uniquely Indian': PV Sindhu praises langur mimicry atrists depolyes to keep monkeys away at BWF World Championships WION
Badminton.body:
India is set to host the BWF World Championships at the Indira Gandhi indoor stadium in New Delhi from August 17-23, 2026 and the organizers have deployed unique solutions to keep the monkeys away. Specialist artists have been hired to mimic langurs to keep the monkeys and other animals away from the fans in the stand. This comes after monkeys disrupted the Indian Open in January earlier this year. Star Indian shutter PV Sindhu, meanwhile, has appreciated the unique solution to ensure safe games.

“You can laugh at the solution, but you have to love the effort. So many people are working behind the scenes to make sure India is ready to welcome the world. Our solutions may be uniquely Indian, but so are our warmth, our spirit and our hospitality. Can’t wait for the badminton world to experience it all in Delhi. See you soon!,” She posted on X with a video of an artist mimicking the voice of langurs to keep the rhesus macaques away.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships: Monkey whisperers to anti-pigeon gel, Delhi leaves nothing to chance
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships: Monkey whisperers to anti-pigeon gel, Delhi leaves nothing to chance The Times of India
Badminton.body:
NEW DELHI: As rain lashed the National Capital Region on Monday afternoon, the message at the Indira Gandhi (IG) indoor stadium in the heart of the city was clear: nothing is to be left to chance now. It is an unusual sight before a major international event: organisers taking media on a guided tour to showcase preparedness. But with badminton’s global elite arriving from Aug 17 to 23, the sports ministry, Sports Authority of India (SAI) and Badminton Association of India (BAI) are determined that the tournament avoids the irritants that had dogged Jan’s India Open at the same venue — pigeon droppings on to the court, stray dogs and simian presence in the stands and stadium complex.

For India, seeking preferred-destination status for global sporting events, the success of a World Championships returning after 17 years carries considerable weight. Among those bestowed with the responsibility to keep things smooth and running is Jabbar — Delhi’s “monkey whisperer” — part of a fourman team that uses langur calls to keep the primates away.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships: Battle-hardened Ayush Shetty is ready
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships: Battle-hardened Ayush Shetty is ready Deccan Herald
Badminton.body:
Bengaluru: Indian shuttlers will look to make the most of the home advantage as New Delhi is set to host the BWF World Championships, starting next Monday. Prominent names like PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen benefited from their higher ranking to a favourable draw but Karnataka’s own Ayush Shetty (in pic) had no such comfort.

The unseeded World No. 23 is pitted against China’s World No. 1 Shi Yuqi on his Worlds debut. The 30-year-old Chinese shuttler is enjoying a psychological advantage over the 21-year-old Mangalorean, with three wins in their all last three outings, including a lopsided victory of 21-8, 21-10 at the Asian Championships in Ningbo, China this April.

Badminton.summary: Mixed Doubles: Top Five Pairs to Watch BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
With the BWF World Championships 2026 fast approaching, what do recent performances indicate? Here is a glimpse of some of the top contenders in mixed doubles: The world No.1 duo will be the pair to beat, for they head to the World Championships having made three straight finals, winning two. Although the season wasn’t all smooth sailing, Feng/Huang rediscovered their best in the run-up to the Worlds. That they have yet to win a World Championships medal as a pair will provide further motivation.

The runners-up from last year and bronze medallists from Copenhagen 2023 have had a somewhat quiet season so far, winning just a Super 300 title in Macau and finishing runners-up at the Malaysia Open. Still, given their track record of going deep in big tournaments, few will rule out Jiang/Wei having another podium finish.

Badminton.title: BAI, SAI give IG Stadium major facelift ahead of BWF World Championships
Badminton.summary: BAI, SAI give IG Stadium major facelift ahead of BWF World Championships ThePrint
Badminton.body:
New Delhi, Aug 10 (PTI) The organisers of the upcoming BWF World Championships in India have taken extensive steps to upgrade the venue, the Indira Gandhi Stadium, to avoid the embarrassment that rocked the India Open earlier this year.

The Badminton Association of India (BAI) and the Sports Authority of India (SAI) — the venue’s owner — learnt their lesson the hard way. During the India Open in January, pigeons twice halted a second-round match between HS Prannoy and Loh Kean Yew. The subsequent complaints regarding hygiene and Delhi’s smog left the BAI in a difficult position.

Badminton.title: Ashmita Chaliha Wins Maiden BWF World Tour Title At Korea Masters 2026
Badminton.summary: Ashmita Chaliha Wins Maiden BWF World Tour Title At Korea Masters 2026 Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
Ashmita Chaliha wins the Korea Masters 2026 to claim her maiden BWF World Tour title, becoming the first Indian to win the Super 300 event. India’s rising badminton star, Ashmita Chaliah made a remarkable comeback to win the Korea Masters 2026. She defeated China’s Han Qianxi 14-21, 21-14, 21-14 in the women’s singles final on Sunday. The victory marked the 26-year-old maiden BWF World Tour title. And she became the first Indian shuttler to win the BWF Super 300 tournament.

Chaliha played her first-ever BWF World Tour final, and had to rebound from her defeat in the opening game to fourth seed Han Qianxi. It began in a confident manner from the Indian side and they led 9-5, but the five-point runs from the Chinese side changed the game, as Han took the opening 21-14. The Indian Badminton player was coming out strong in the second game. Unaffected, Chaliha took advantage of her put and took the advantage away with a 21-14 win at the halfway point and ended the game.

Badminton.title: Peru Para: Triple Crown for Pilar Jaurequi
Badminton.summary: Peru Para: Triple Crown for Pilar Jaurequi BWF
Badminton.body:
Pilar Jauregui emerged the most successful athlete at the Peru Para Badminton International 2026, winning all her three events to help Peru win seven titles and finish just behind Brazil in the overall standings.

The home icon won her Wheelchair (WH2) singles after opponent Annika Schroeder retired after the first game; Jaurequi then teamed up with Jaquelin Burgos for the women’s doubles WH1-WH2 final, which they won beating Brazil’s Ana Gomes/Milani Maria Silva Gomes 21-9 21-11.

Badminton.title: Ashmita Chaliha clinches maiden BWF World Tour title at Korea Masters
Badminton.summary: Ashmita Chaliha clinches maiden BWF World Tour title at Korea Masters WION
Badminton.body:
India’s Ashmita Chaliha clinched her first BWF World Tour title after beating China’s fourth-seeded Han Qian Xi in the women’s singles final of the Korea Masters Super 300 in Asan on Sunday (Aug 9). The 26-year-old from Assam recovered from a slow start and held her nerve in a closely contested decider to win 14-21, 21-14, 21-14 in 53 minutes.

During the match, Ashmita started the opening game well, taking an early 3-0 lead and later moving 9-5 ahead, however, Han fought back strongly and levelled the score at 11-11. The Chinese player then took control with a run of points and comfortably closed out the game 21-14.

Badminton.title: Korea Masters: Maiden Titles for Zhu, Chaliha
Badminton.summary: Korea Masters: Maiden Titles for Zhu, Chaliha BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Zhu Xuan Chen and Ashmita Chaliha won their first HSBC BWF World Tour titles at the VICTOR Korea Masters 2026 in Asan today. Zhu held off a strong charge from home hope Yoo Tae Bin in the second game, saving three game points to win 21-16 23-21, while Chaliha recovered from a first game deficit to beat Han Qian Xi 14-21 21-14 21-14.

Both Zhu and Chaliha were playing their first World Tour final. “I’m really happy,” said world No.68 Zhu. “I don’t think I played particularly well in the previous two tournaments, and my form has been quite up and down this year. So to be able to win the title at this tournament, I’m really happy with the result.

Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha scripted a memorable chapter in her career as she won her maiden BWF World Tour title with a stunning comeback victory over China's Han Qianxi in the women's singles final of the Korea Masters Super 300.

The 26-year-old from Guwahati overcame a slow start to beat Han 14-21, 21-14, 21-14 in a 53-minute final, underlining her resilience and fighting spirit on the biggest day of her career.

Badminton.title: Korea Masters: Chaliha Earns Title Shot
Badminton.summary: Korea Masters: Chaliha Earns Title Shot BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
World No.50 Ashmita Chaliha made her first HSBC BWF World Tour final at the VICTOR Korea Masters 2026 today beating compatriot Rakshita Sree Santhosh Ramraj. Chaliha, whose previous best this year was the semifinals of the Macau Open in June, prevailed in a hard battle with Santhosh Ramraj, 21-13 16-21 21-13.

Chaliha has had an impressive road to the final. She first beat qualifier Ririna Hiramoto, then Kim Min Ji, both in straight games, before edging top seed Hina Akechi 20-22 21-15 21-19 in the quarterfinals.

Badminton.title: BWF Korea Masters 2026: Yoo Taebin Breaks Into World Top 50 After Reaching Final
Badminton.summary: BWF Korea Masters 2026: Yoo Taebin Breaks Into World Top 50 After Reaching Final Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
Yoo Taebin reaches the men’s singles final at the BWF Korea Masters 2026, securing his debut in the world top 50 after a stunning semi-final win. Republic of Korea’s Yoo Taebin has secured a major career milestone at the BWF Korea Masters 2026, reaching the men’s singles final on home soil and guaranteeing his debut inside the world top 50 when the rankings are updated next week. The 22-year-old produced one of the biggest results of the tournament by defeating top seed Okimoto Yudai of Japan 21-16, 21-18 in Saturday’s semi-final.

Since the win, Yoo Taebin is one of the most noteworthy players in the Korea Masters 2026. He has now gone into his second consecutive Super 300 final as a No.1 Seeded player. The victory is Yoo's latest success as he has climbed much higher in international badminton and last week finished runner-up at the Taipei Open. His win over Okimoto, the top single seed male that entered the tournament, was all the more brilliant. With his rank of 2nd finalized, Yoo Taebin will now have a guaranteed spot in the world top 50 for the first time. This is definitely a milestone for the young south Korean and now he can take the chance to win his first Super 300.

Badminton.title: Ashmita Chaliha continues giant-killing run, reaches maiden BWF World Tour final
Badminton.summary: Ashmita Chaliha continues giant-killing run, reaches maiden BWF World Tour final India Today
Badminton.body:
Ashmita Chaliha continued her impressive comeback at the Korea Masters Super 300, overcoming teenage compatriot Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj 21-13, 16-21, 21-13 in a 48-minute semifinal to reach her maiden BWF World Tour final in Iksan on Saturday.

The 26-year-old Indian, who returned to competition in May after a three-month layoff following a medial meniscus tear in her right knee, has now put together another significant run on the BWF Tour. Her campaign includes a stunning quarterfinal victory over top seed and world No. 22 Hina Akechi of Japan.

Badminton.title: India's Contingent Aims for Success at BWF World Championships
Badminton.summary: India's Contingent Aims for Success at BWF World Championships India News Network
Badminton.body:
India will be represented by a squad of 14 shuttlers at the BWF World Championships, commencing next week at New Delhi's Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium. The tournament marks a significant opportunity for the Indian team to continue a medal-winning streak that dates back to 2011. Since the event's inception, India has secured 15 medals—10 bronze, four silver, and one gold. P.V. Sindhu remains India's only world champion, having won the title in 2019, and is also the most decorated player at the Championships with five medals: one gold, two silver, and two bronze, a record she shares with Zhang Ning of China.

India has reached the podium in every edition since 2011, with the men's doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty winning bronze in 2025. The Indian contingent, enjoying home support, will aim to uphold this impressive tradition. The squad includes two entries each in men's singles, men's doubles, women's singles, and mixed doubles, alongside one women's doubles pair.

Badminton.title: ‘Quality of Top 20 is What Top 10 Used to Be’
Badminton.summary: ‘Quality of Top 20 is What Top 10 Used to Be’ bwfworldchampionships.bwfbadminton.com
Badminton.body:
Ahead of the upcoming BWF World Championships – her 11th – European champion Kirsty Gilmour talks about adapting to younger generations of opponents, working on becoming the best version of herself, and her connection with Indian fans.

You’ve seen different generations of opponents. What do you make of the younger ones? Is there a different approach or is it just various individual styles as before? Year on year it becomes more physical. Maybe when I was younger, I thought I would get to a point and then it would become easier. I would like ‘get it’ but because the game is always evolving, always changing, it’s never become easier to be honest, and I think the younger ones are so hungry to beat the more established players, whereas before maybe the older ones dominated, but the younger ones are always at your heels, always ready.

Badminton.title: 'Completely transformed': BAI promises best-ever BWF World Championships after India Open controversy
Badminton.summary: 'Completely transformed': BAI promises best-ever BWF World Championships after India Open controversy The Times of India
Badminton.body:
NEW DELHI: Months after the India Open came under fire over the condition of its facilities, the Badminton Association of India (BAI) has assured players and fans that New Delhi's Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium has undergone a complete makeover and is ready to host the "best-ever" edition of the BWF World Championships.

The World Championships will be held in the national capital from August 17, with organisers confident that the issues which overshadowed the India Open earlier this year have now been fully addressed.
Badminton.copy:

The World Championships will be held in the national capital from August 17, with organisers confident that the issues which overshadowed the India Open earlier this year have now been fully addressed.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships 2026 draw: Ayush Shetty to face Shi Yuqi in first round; PV Sindhu, Lakshya Sen get easy opener
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships 2026 draw: Ayush Shetty to face Shi Yuqi in first round; PV Sindhu, Lakshya Sen get easy opener WION
Badminton.body:
India's medal contenders got a mixed draw for the BWF World Championships 2026, set to be held at the Indira Gandhi Stadium in New Delhi from August 17 to 23. The biggest opening-round contest features Asian Championships silver medallist Ayush Shetty, who faces defending champion and world no. 1 Shi Yuqi of China. Former world champion PV Sindhu starts her campaign against Ireland's Sophia Nobel, currently ranked world no. 141, while Lakshya Sen will take on Austria's Collins Valentine Filimon in the men's singles first round. If he advances, Lakshya could meet second seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn of Thailand in the pre-quarterfinals.

India's top men's doubles pair, fifth seeds Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, have received a first-round bye. They will open their campaign against either Scotland's Alexander Dunn and Adam Pringle or Thailand's Chaloempon Charoenkitamorn and Worrapol Thongsa-Nga. India is hosting the BWF World Championships for the first time in 17 years. The official draw ceremony was held in New Delhi on Wednesday. Badminton Association of India General Secretary Sanjay Mishra revealed that more than ₹20 crore has been invested in upgrading the Indira Gandhi Multipurpose Indoor Stadium, expressing confidence that the event would set new benchmarks for world badminton.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships draw: Ayush Shetty handed tough test against world No. 1 Shi Yu Qi in opener
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships draw: Ayush Shetty handed tough test against world No. 1 Shi Yu Qi in opener The Times of India
Badminton.body:
NEW DELHI: The road to a home World Championships podium could hardly be tougher for rising star Ayush Shetty after the BWF World Championships draw, announced here on Wednesday, pitched the unseeded Indian against defending champion, top seed and World No. 1 Shi Yu Qi of China in a riveting opening round clash. The tournament will be held at the IGI Stadium from Aug 17 to 23.

Ayush, who lost to Shi in this year’s Badminton Asia Championships final, gets an opportunity to avenge that defeat. Chief national coach Pullela Gopichand felt the daunting opener could yet work in the youngster’s favour. “I do believe Ayush is very good and with his attacking style, playing Shi in the first round is better than meeting him later. If he wins, it opens up the draw,” Gopichand said, adding, “Overall, it looks like a good draw from the Indian perspective. We aspire to end up on the podium in a few events.”

New Delhi, Aug 5 (PTI) The Badminton World Federation on Wednesday expressed satisfaction with the extensive renovation and cleaning work carried out at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium here ahead of the World Championships, saying most of the shortcomings highlighted after the India Open earlier this year have been addressed.

Badminton.summary: Match-fixing probe casts shadow over Indonesia’s badminton World C’ships campaign The Straits Times
Badminton.body:
PETALING JAYA – The Badminton Association of Indonesia (PBSI) has withdrawn two mixed doubles pairs from the upcoming World Championships amid a match-fixing investigation by the sport’s world governing body.

The two pairings are world No. 13 Jafar Hidayatullah-Felisha Pasaribu and world No. 24 Adnan Maulana-Indah Cahya Sari Jamil. Although there has been no official confirmation linking the pairs to the probe, their withdrawal from the tournament, which will be held from Aug 17 to Aug 23 in New Delhi, has fuelled speculation.

Badminton.title: BWF’s 15-Point Badminton Scoring System Set To Transform The Sport From 2027
Badminton.summary: BWF’s 15-Point Badminton Scoring System Set To Transform The Sport From 2027 Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
The BWF 15-point format will replace the 21-point scoring system from 2027. Here's how the change could impact tactics, player endurance, and match outcomes. The Badminton World Federation has announced one of the biggest changes in the history of the . BWF is going to introduce a 15-point format from 2027. The new format will replace the long standing 21 point system. The change is made after considering the aim to reduce player fatigue, shorten match duration and make contests more exciting for audiences. While officials believe the badminton rule changes will modernise the , players. Coaches are still divided over its long-term impact on competition and strategy.

The changes implemented in the 15-point badminton format making it the latest sports news development, mean that games will be played down to 15 points rather than 21 instead of the previous 21-point games. The shorter version is anticipated to reduce physical strain on the athlete, many of whom may play in several tournaments yearly, the BWF said. But with the new rules for badminton scoring, slower starts and unforced errors will leave players with much more time to recover. Each challenge will have a higher value attached to it and players will need to be tougher from the first serve from the outset. The games will also be shorter, which will reduce needless set-up delays that sprawl and end up interfering with the action to viewers watching at home on television and streaming online for fast paced sporting action.

Badminton.title: Badminton: Indonesian pairs withdraw from worlds amid match-fixing probe
Badminton.summary: Badminton: Indonesian pairs withdraw from worlds amid match-fixing probe The Star
Badminton.body:
PETALING JAYA: Indonesia’s world No. 13 mixed doubles pair Jafar Hidayatullah-Felisha Pasaribu have come under the spotlight following an alleged match-fixing investigation involving several Indonesian players.

Although there has been no official confirmation linking the pair to the case, their withdrawal from the tournament has fuelled speculation. The Indonesian Badminton Association (PBSI) secretary-general Ricky Soebagdja said in a statement that Jafar-Felisha, as well as another mixed doubles pair, Adnan Maulana-Indah Cahya Sari Jamil, had been withdrawn as part of adjustments to Indonesia’s squad for the World Championships.

Badminton.title: Justin prepared to adapt in India for BWF World Championships
Badminton.summary: Justin prepared to adapt in India for BWF World Championships The Sun Malaysia
Badminton.body:
National shuttler Justin Hoh says he is ready to adapt to conditions in India as he prepares for his debut at the 2026 BWF World Championships. NATIONAL men’s singles shuttler Justin Hoh is ready to adapt to whatever conditions he may face at his maiden appearance at the 2026 BWF World Championships in New Delhi from Aug 17 to 23.

The 22-year-old said he did not want to dwell on the competition venue’s conditions and was instead focused on making the best possible preparations for the prestigious tournament.

Competitor News.title: Market news
Competitor News.body:
According to Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, chief executive Ryan Cohen is considering proposing a partnership or joint venture that would enable eBay to leverage GameStop’s roughly 1,600 US retail locations.

Sources told Bloomberg that such a move could allow both to increase market share in high-margin categories such as trading cards and collectibles. It was understood that GameStop, as one of eBay’s largest shareholders, would seek representation on eBay’s board as part of any partnership.

Competitor News.title: Racing Santander close in on Julen Agirrezabala deal
Competitor News.summary: Racing Santander close in on Julen Agirrezabala deal Yahoo Sports
Competitor News.body:
Racing Santander have reached a verbal agreement with Athletic Club to sign goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala, according to comuniate.com. The move would see the Rentería-born keeper leave Bilbao to become Racing's new number one as the Cantabrian club prepares for its return to LaLiga EA Sports.

Agirrezabala has spent much of his Athletic career behind Unai Simón, though he has shown flashes of real quality when called upon, particularly in the Copa del Rey and Europa League. Last season he went out on loan to Valencia, where injuries disrupted his campaign and prevented him from establishing himself as an undisputed starter.

Competitor News.title: Liverpool in new shirt sponsor talks: Standard Chartered deal up in 2027
Competitor News.summary: Liverpool in new shirt sponsor talks: Standard Chartered deal up in 2027 This Is Anfield
Competitor News.body:
Liverpool officials are in talks with potential sponsors as their front-of-shirt and shirt-sleeve deals with Standard Chartered and Expedia will expire in 2027. This could be the final season with Liverpool wearing Standard Chartered on the front of their shirts, with the British multinational bank having sponsored the club since 2010.

Liverpool’s current agreement runs to the end of 2026/27 and is worth around £50 million a year, after an extension was signed in 2022. The same applies to shirt-sleeve sponsor Expedia, who took over from Western Union in 2020 and last agreed terms in 2023 at a projected value of £12 million per season.

Competitor News.title: #DONKOMI: Yan Diomande joins Real Madrid on seven year deal
Competitor News.summary: #DONKOMI: Yan Diomande joins Real Madrid on seven year deal citisportsonline.com
Competitor News.body:
Côte d’Ivoire winger Yan Diomande has completed a move to Spanish giants Real Madrid from German Bundesliga side RB Leipzig. Real Madrid announced the signing on Thursday, August 6, bringing an end to lengthy negotiations that had at one stage appeared to stall.

The 19-year-old has signed a seven-year contract until 2033 in a deal reportedly worth €125 million, with a further €15 million in performance related add ons. Diomande is regarded as one of football’s brightest young talents, with Liverpool also reportedly interested in signing him during the transfer window.
